record.narrative: No assessments are due, so no claim statuses are changed at this stage. I selected the 12 currently active, previously registered, but untested comparisons because they are the highest-value follow-ups to the accepted core associations and to the MAPK/co-driver/stress-response hypotheses registered in the previous explore stage. H141 and H142 directly test effect modification of the accepted PTEN-loss/dependency_STAT3 association by high IFN-gamma signature and by low Cas9 activity. H132 and H133 test whether the same PTEN-loss/STAT3 effect is robust in high-EMT and high-stemness contexts. H136 and H139 test accepted TP53-loss/dependency_USP7 and MYC-expression-context dependency_DHX9 questions in focused transcriptomic contexts. H143 and H144 test whether KRAS mutation is associated with weaker dependency_BRAF and weaker dependency_EGFR in high-quality high-Cas9 screens, a MAPK-bypass specificity test. H145 tests whether PTEN loss associates with stronger KRAS dependency among KRAS-wild-type high-quality screens. H146 tests whether PIK3CA mutation phenocopies the PTEN-loss STAT3 association among PTEN-intact high-quality screens. H147 tests whether TP53 loss is associated with stronger WRN dependency after removing MSI-high status under technically stringent conditions. H148 tests whether MYC amplification has a transcription-output-dependent effect on dependency_POLR2A after broadly near-null MYC-amplification results. Returned estimates and intervals will already be signed to each registered direction; positive values support the registered hypothesis. I will judge scientific meaningfulness against approximate 10%-of-population-scale benchmarks for the relevant dependency outcome and will treat all conclusions as observational within this supplied dataset.

Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: I judged each new result against approximate 10%-of-population absolute dependency benchmarks: STAT3/EMT/stemness contexts about +0.028, USP7 about +0.018, KRAS/EGFR/BRAF/POLR2A/DHX9 about +0.025, and WRN about +0.030 for signed positive support. All intervals are signed to the registered claim direction, so positive signed values support the hypothesis. H132 and H133 show large positive PTEN-loss/STAT3 effects in high-EMT and high-stemness eligibility groups, with signed lower bounds +0.261 and +0.156, respectively, far above the STAT3 benchmark. These are unadjusted dataset-specific associations within selected phenotype contexts; eligibility variables are pre-outcome covariates, so there is no direct outcome leakage, but EMT/stemness may correlate with PTEN-loss biology or selection, so I accept these as robust contextual associations rather than causal or generalizable claims. H136 similarly supports TP53-loss/USP7 in high-AXL lines with signed estimate +0.267 and lower bound +0.118, far above the USP7 benchmark, so I accept it and close it as a strong context-specific replication of the accepted TP53-loss/USP7 association. H132 is active and validated because the high-EMT top-quartile selection resembles the earlier high-IFN discovery context whose validated effect was materially attenuated; independent confirmation is useful before treating H132 as a stable separate context. H133 is accepted but closed given its large discovery lower bound and the fact that the broader PTEN-loss/STAT3 effect is already validated in multiple contexts. H139 rejects the claimed DHX9 effect in high-MYC expression lines: signed estimate -0.016, signed upper bound +0.017, below the DHX9 benchmark. H141 and H142 both registered positive interaction expectations, but the signed intervals are entirely negative: H141 -0.212 (-0.331 to -0.094) and H142 -0.149 (-0.271 to -0.027). For the registered positive claims, these are rejections. H141 is scientifically interesting because it is a large opposite-sign interaction: high IFN-gamma may attenuate rather than amplify PTEN-loss-associated STAT3 dependency, despite the strong high-IFN main effect. However, reversal after a prespecified wrong direction is susceptible to multiplicity and subgroup selection, so I registered a reversed interaction proposal as unresolved rather than accepting it. H142's opposite interaction is in a low-Cas9 subgroup, where assay-quality confounding is plausible, so I close it rather than prioritize a reversal. H143 rejects a clinically meaningful positive KRAS-mutation/BRAF relationship in high-quality, high-Cas9 screens because the signed upper bound +0.017 is below the BRAF benchmark; the small negative point estimate does not support a meaningful opposite effect under the registered scale. H144, H145, H147, and H148 remain unresolved but closed: their point estimates are near null, and their intervals cannot exclude clinically meaningful effects in the claimed direction, so there is insufficient evidence to accept, but also too much upper-bound uncertainty to reject cleanly. H146 rejects PIK3CA mutation as a phenocopy of PTEN loss for STAT3 dependency among PTEN-intact high-quality screens because the signed upper bound +0.013 is below the STAT3 benchmark. Overall, the accepted core remains SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2, KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2, TP53-loss/USP7, MSI-high/WRN, and PTEN-loss/STAT3, now with several additional accepted context-specific PTEN-loss/STAT3 and TP53-loss/USP7 datasets, but these remain observational within the supplied dataset. I requested validation for H132 only.

record.narrative: All returned estimates and intervals are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction, so positive signed values support the accepted/registered direction. The benchmark used for scientific meaningfulness is approximately the population-scale 10% absolute dependency-score difference, around +0.028 for dependency_STAT3 and dependency_USP7 after sign transformation. H113 passes the response deadline: among TP53-loss lines, PTEN loss is associated with stronger dependency_STAT3. Discovery signed effect was +0.190 (interval +0.085 to +0.296), and independent adjusted validation signed effect was +0.252 (interval +0.071 to +0.434). The validation lower bound is well above the approximate STAT3 benchmark, so I accept and close H113. This supports a co-occurring TP53-loss context association in the supplied dataset, not causal mediation or generalizability. H109 also passes: among high screen-quality and high-Cas9 screens, PTEN loss is associated with stronger dependency_STAT3. Discovery signed effect was +0.236 (interval +0.142 to +0.331); validation signed effect was +0.203 (interval +0.040 to +0.366). The validation lower bound is above the STAT3 benchmark, though closer to it, so I accept and close H109 as a robust dataset-specific association under technically stringent screening conditions. H132 is the new validation: among high-EMT lines, PTEN loss is associated with stronger dependency_STAT3. Discovery signed effect was +0.378 (interval +0.261 to +0.495); validation signed effect was +0.262 (interval +0.084 to +0.441). The validated lower bound exceeds the STAT3 benchmark, so I accept and close H132. The validation effect is materially smaller than discovery, similar to the high-IFN-gamma context, indicating possible discovery-context inflation, but the independent interval still supports a clinically meaningful dataset-specific association in high-EMT lines. I did not newly accept H149, the post-hoc reversed IFN interaction claim. Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous

The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link

Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without

Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,

comparison cell.

is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released

the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.

the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.

changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative: No assessments are due, so I do not change any existing claim statuses. I register a new set of falsifiable follow-up comparisons rather than refinements, to avoid missing motivating-evidence links and to broaden the evidence base around accepted dataset-specific associations. The WRN proposals ask whether the accepted MSI-high association remains strong in technically stringent screens with mutation burden below the top quartile, and whether it persists in TP53-loss lines. The first would support an MSI-context effect rather than a generic mutation-burden proxy; the second would test whether p53 context coexists with, rather than explains, the MSI signal. The STAT3 proposals test PTEN-loss-associated stronger STAT3 dependency in technically stringent low-IFN-gamma lines, high-MYC-expression lines, and high-AXL-expression lines. These probe whether the broad PTEN-loss/STAT3 association is robust in expression contexts with potentially distinct transcriptional, RTK, inflammatory, or Cas9-quality biology. The KRAS/receptor proposals test pathway-bypass specificity: among KRAS-wild-type high-quality lines, BRAF V600E is expected to show weaker KRAS dependency if downstream activation bypasses KRAS, while EGFR amplification is expected to show stronger KRAS dependency if upstream receptor signaling feeds through RAS. Conversely, among KRAS-mutant lines, EGFR and ERBB2 dependency should be weaker if KRAS mutation bypasses those receptor nodes. The NFE2L2 proposal tests whether the accepted KEAP1-loss-associated weaker dependency persists in TP53-loss lines, where co-loss may change oxidative-stress and p53-associated survival biology. The non-Avana high-quality robustness tests ask whether the very strong SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 and TP53-loss/USP7 associations survive in screens with a different library, controlling for high screen ROC quality. I use approximate 10% population-scale dependency-score benchmarks for each outcome. For dependency_STAT3 and dependency_USP7, a benchmark is about 0.028; for dependency_KRAS, dependency_EGFR, dependency_BRAF, and dependency_WRN, about 0.025-0.030; for dependency_SMARCA2 and dependency_NFE2L2, the effects are expected to be very large if real. A proposal will be considered scientifically meaningful only if the signed estimate and lower interval bound support the registered direction near or above these thresholds. All claims remain observational within the supplied dataset and are not interpreted as causal or generalizable.

First, it probes effect modification and complement contexts around the accepted PTEN-loss/STAT3 and TP53-loss/USP7 associations: H150 gives the low-IFN complement main effect needed to interpret the high-IFN interaction; H151 tests the high-EMT interaction after validated attenuation of the high-EMT main effect; H152 tests whether high AXL expression modifies TP53-loss-associated USP7 dependency; H154 tests the PTEN-loss/STAT3 association under stringent low-IFN screening conditions. Second, it tests MAPK pathway bypass specificity: H157 and H158 ask whether KRAS dependency in KRAS-wild-type high-quality screens is altered by BRAF V600E or EGFR amplification, while H159 and H160 ask whether EGFR or ERBB2 dependency is weaker among KRAS-mutant lines as expected if KRAS mutation bypasses receptor nodes. record.narrative: All intervals are already signed to the registered direction, so positive values support the claim. I used approximate 10% population-scale absolute dependency-score benchmarks for acceptance: roughly +0.028 for STAT3-type effects, +0.025 to +0.026 for KRAS/EGFR/ERBB2-type effects, +0.030 for WRN, and +0.017 to +0.018 for USP7; very large effects were accepted when the lower bound was far above benchmark. H150 and H154 accept strongly: PTEN loss is associated with much stronger dependency_STAT3 in the low-IFN complement and in technically stringent low-IFN screens, with signed lower bounds +0.152 and +0.098 respectively, well above benchmark. These are robust dataset-specific context associations, not causal claims. H153 accepts: the MSI-high dependency_WRN association remains very strong even in high-quality screens with mutation burden below the top quartile, lower bound +0.761, supporting an MSI context rather than a generic mutation-burden proxy. H161 accepts: the KEAP1-loss-associated weaker NFE2L2 dependency persists in TP53-loss lines, lower bound +0.763. H163 accepts the very strong SMARCA4-loss-associated dependency_SMARCA2 effect in non-Avana high-quality screens, lower bound +0.690, despite modest cell counts. H151 and H152 are unresolved but deferred: the high-EMT PTEN-loss STAT3 interaction and high-AXL TP53-loss USP7 interaction have large point estimates but signed lower bounds of only +0.011 and +0.008, below clinically meaningful thresholds. They may reflect effect modification, but multiplicity, subgroup selection, and dependence on discovery-only interaction estimates prevent acceptance. H157 is unresolved and closed because the BRAF V600E effect on dependency_KRAS in KRAS-wild-type high-quality screens is near null with broad uncertainty. H158 and H160 reject the registered positive directions: EGFR amplification does not support clinically meaningful stronger dependency_KRAS in KRAS-wild-type screens, and ERBB2 amplification does not support clinically meaningful stronger dependency_ERBB2 among KRAS mutants; signed upper bounds fall below the relevant benchmarks. H159 rejects the registered positive direction but the signed interval is entirely negative and clinically meaningful in the opposite direction, suggesting EGFR amplification may be associated with stronger dependency_EGFR among KRAS mutants in this dataset. Because this reversal was discovered after seeing the wrong-signed original interaction and has no independent validation, I did not accept it automatically; I registered a new reversed proposal as unresolved and parented it to H159. H164 is unresolved and closed because the non-Avana high-quality TP53-loss USP7 signal is underpowered, with an interval crossing zero. H149 is left status unresolved but investigation closed: the reversed high-IFN interaction has a strong discovery interval, but validation of the high-IFN main effect was attenuated, and independent confirmation of the interaction is lacking. No validation was requested because no new validation requests remain. All conclusions remain observational within the supplied dataset and do not establish causality or generalizability.

Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.

the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.

evidence assessment.

The first would support an MSI-context effect rather than a generic mutation-burden proxy; the second would test whether p53 context coexists with, rather than explains, the MSI signal. The STAT3 proposals test PTEN-loss-associated stronger STAT3 dependency in technically stringent low-IFN-gamma lines, high-MYC-expression lines, and high-AXL-expression lines. record.narrative: All intervals are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction, so positive signed values support the registered direction. H123 now has independent validation. For PTEN-loss versus PTEN-intact lines with high IFN-gamma signature, the discovery signed association with stronger dependency_STAT3 was +0.423 (interval +0.319 to +0.527). The independent adjusted validation signed effect was +0.193 with lower bound +0.045 and upper bound +0.340. Using the approximate 10% population-scale benchmark for STAT3 of about +0.028, the validated lower bound is above the clinical-meaningfulness threshold, so I accept and close H123. The validation effect is materially attenuated relative to discovery, which is consistent with some context inflation in the high-IFN-gamma discovery estimate, but the independent interval still supports a scientifically meaningful dataset-specific PTEN-loss/STAT3 association in that context. I am closing H151 and H152 as unresolved because their signed lower bounds (+0.011 and +0.008, respectively) are below the relevant 10% benchmarks and validation requests are exhausted. I am also closing H165 as unresolved because the reversed EGFR-amplification/KRAS-mutant EGFR-dependency signal is post hoc and the lower bound is too close to zero for confident acceptance. The supported dataset-specific core remains: SMARCA4 loss is associated with markedly stronger SMARCA2 dependency; KEAP1 loss is associated with markedly weaker NFE2L2 dependency; TP53 loss is associated with markedly weaker USP7 dependency; MSI-high status is associated with markedly stronger WRN dependency; and PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency across broad and several constrained contexts, now including the validated high-IFN-gamma context. Negative or unsupported findings include clinically meaningful null results for most receptor/MAPK and MYC-amplification hypotheses, no canonical TP53-loss/MDM2 effect, no stable PTEN-loss effect on KRAS dependency among KRAS-mutant lines, no supported MSI-high effect on POLR2A, and no meaningful constructed-marker effects. The most informative next analyses are robustness checks in technically stringent screens for the accepted PTEN-loss/STAT3 contexts (high IFN, high EMT, and high stemness) and for TP53-loss/USP7 in high AXL expression, while retaining active complement/context tests for PTEN-loss/STAT3 under high MYC or high AXL and MSI-high/WRN under TP53 loss. All conclusions remain observational within the supplied dataset and do not establish causality or generalizability.

Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative: No assessments are due, so I do not change any existing claim statuses. I registered twelve new comparisons aimed at two goals: robustness of the accepted dataset-specific associations under additional biological and technical contexts, and follow-up of one still-ambiguous RB1/KIF18A pathway signal. For accepted associations, returned estimates are already signed to the registered direction, so positive values support the registered hypothesis. The main alternative explanations I consider are context-specific attenuation, multiplicity/subgroup selection, technical confounding, or small-cell instability. I avoid stacking multiple stringent QC filters in rare-exposure contexts because that can make exposed cells fall below 20; instead each context uses either high Cas9 activity or high screen ROC plus a slow-growth context. The STAT3 proposals ask whether PTEN-loss-associated stronger dependency_STAT3 remains clinically meaningful in high interferon, EMT, stemness, MYC, AXL, and high-serum contexts. The USP7 proposals ask whether TP53-loss-associated weaker USP7 dependency remains in high AXL and high MYC contexts. The SMARCA2 proposal asks whether the very strong SMARCA4-loss signal remains in high-quality slow-growing screens, reducing concern that the signal is driven by fast-growing lines or screening quality. The NFE2L2 proposals ask whether the strong KEAP1-loss-associated weaker NFE2L2 dependency persists in high-interferon and high-quality slow-growing contexts. The RB1 proposal retests RB1-loss-associated dependency_KIF18A under combined high screen quality and high Cas9 activity, because the earlier screen-quality-only result was directionally favorable but not decisive. I will judge acceptance against approximate 10% population-scale thresholds for the outcome: about 0.028 for dependency_STAT3, 0.018 for dependency_USP7, 0.042 for dependency_SMARCA2, 0.009 for dependency_NFE2L2, 0.026 for dependency_KIF18A, and about 0.030 for dependency_WRN. Effects with point estimates but lower bounds below these thresholds will remain unresolved rather than accepted, and all conclusions remain observational within the supplied dataset, not causal or necessarily generalizable.

Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,

is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator

For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.

record.narrative: No assessments are due, so I make no status changes to existing claims. I request 12 previously registered, currently unevaluated analyses selected for high scientific value. H100 is a priority interaction: PTEN loss showed a positive discovery association with dependency_KRAS in KRAS-mutant lines in H89, but independent validation reversed that result; H100 directly tests whether the PTEN-loss effect differs by KRAS-mutation status. H162 tests whether the accepted very strong MSI-high/dependency_WRN association persists within TP53-loss lines, though the exposed cell is likely near the minimum and will be interpreted cautiously. For PTEN-loss/STAT3, I request high-quality-screen context main effects for AXL-high H156, high IFN H166, high EMT H167, and high stemness H168, complementing the broadly accepted PTEN-loss/STAT3 association and the validated but attenuated high-IFN effect. For TP53-loss/USP7, I request high AXL with high screen quality H169, high AXL with high Cas9 H175, and high MYC with high Cas9 H176, because TP53-loss/USP7 is accepted broadly but AXL showed an unresolved interaction. I also request robustness/follow-up tests for SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 in slow-growing high-quality screens H177, KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 in high IFN with high Cas9 H178, and the ambiguous RB1-loss/dependency_KIF18A signal under high screen quality and high Cas9 H179. Returned intervals will already be signed to the registered direction, so positive signed values support the registered hypothesis; acceptance will require lower bounds to exceed outcome-specific approximate 10% population-scale benchmarks, and small-cell context estimates will be handled conservatively. No validation can be requested because voluntary validation requests are exhausted. All conclusions will remain observational within this supplied dataset and will not be treated as causal or generally reproducible unless supported.

Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: All returned intervals are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction, so positive signed values support the registered direction. I used approximate 10% population-scale absolute dependency-score benchmarks for acceptance: about 0.028 for STAT3, 0.018 for USP7, 0.026 for KIF18A, 0.030 for WRN, 0.042 for SMARCA2, 0.009 for NFE2L2, and 0.025 to 0.030 for KRAS/BRAF/EGFR/ERBB2-type scores. Acceptance required a valid lower bound above the relevant benchmark and sufficient consistency with prior evidence. H100 remains unresolved and closed: the PTEN-loss/KRAS-mutant interaction on dependency_KRAS is positive (+0.066), but its signed lower bound is only +0.016, below the KRAS benchmark, and it conflicts with the failed independent validation of the simpler PTEN-loss-in-KRAS-mutant main effect H89. This is suggestive of possible effect modification but not clinically meaningful with uncertainty, and no validation remains. H156, H166, H167, and H168 are accepted as dataset-specific context associations: PTEN loss is associated with clinically stronger dependency_STAT3 in high-quality screens with high AXL, high IFN-gamma, high EMT, or high stemness, with signed lower bounds +0.086, +0.185, +0.164, and +0.115 respectively, all well above the STAT3 benchmark. These are observational subgroup associations and may be context-specific or influenced by selection on measured features. H162 is accepted despite an exposed cell of 24 because the MSI-high dependency_WRN association within TP53-loss lines is extremely strong, signed lower bound +0.765, far above the WRN benchmark; it supports persistence of the MSI/WRN signal in a TP53-loss context rather than a TP53-loss-specific effect. H169, H175, and H176 are accepted: TP53 loss is associated with clinically weaker dependency_USP7 in high AXL and high MYC contexts under technical QC, with signed lower bounds +0.165, +0.109, and +0.257, all far above the USP7 benchmark. These are consistent with the broad TP53-loss/USP7 association, although the earlier AXL interaction H152 was not itself decisive. H177 and H178 are accepted: SMARCA4 loss remains very strongly associated with stronger SMARCA2 dependency in slow-growing high-quality screens (lower +0.752), and KEAP1 loss remains very strongly associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency in high IFN-gamma/high Cas9 screens (lower +0.713). Both have small exposed cells but enormous effects. H179 remains unresolved and closed: RB1 loss in high-quality/high-Cas9 screens gives a near-zero signed estimate for dependency_KIF18A, interval -0.057 to +0.052, which is too imprecise to support the registered direction and too wide to rule out a clinically meaningful effect. No validation was requested because voluntary validation requests are exhausted. All conclusions remain observational within the supplied lung-line dataset and do not establish causality or generalizability.

Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator

Final synthesis of the run so far: the strongest, repeatedly supported dataset-specific associations are (1) SMARCA4 loss is associated with markedly stronger SMARCA2 dependency, robust across global, adenocarcinoma, high screen quality, high Cas9 activity, low-growth, MYC-high, PTEN-loss, and ARID1A-loss contexts; (2) KEAP1 loss is associated with markedly weaker/less-negative NFE2L2 dependency, with discovery and independent validation concordant and robust across multiple contexts; (3) TP53 loss is associated with markedly weaker USP7 dependency, validated and reproducible in broad and several QC/biology-restricted contexts; (4) MSI-high is associated with markedly stronger WRN dependency, validated and robust including within high-quality, TP53-loss, and mutation-burden-selected settings; and (5) PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency, supported broadly, through multiple technical and biological contexts, and validated in high-IFN-gamma and high-EMT settings. Negative or unsupported findings include clinically meaningful null results for most direct receptor-tyrosine-kinase amplification effects on their own dependency scores: BRAF V600E did not support dependency_BRAF; EGFR amplification did not produce a robust self-dependency effect; ERBB2 amplification was near-null for dependency_ERBB2 and dependency_STAT3. record.narrative:
I reassessed the due validation for H132 and accept it as a supported, dataset-specific association. The claim tests whether PTEN loss is associated with a more negative, i.e. stronger, dependency_STAT3 score among lines with high EMT score (emt_score >= 0.66). Returned estimates are already signed to the negative claim direction, so positive values support the claim. The discovery estimate was +0.378 (95% Welch interval +0.261 to +0.495), and the independent validation estimate was +0.262 (adjusted interval +0.084 to +0.441). The validation is meaningfully attenuated, but its lower bound still exceeds the approximate 10% population-scale STAT3 benchmark of about 0.028 used in this run and remains far from null. Therefore I accept and close H132, while noting that the smaller validation estimate suggests some discovery-context inflation and that the inference remains observational within the supplied lung-line dataset.

Final synthesis of the run so far: the strongest, repeatedly supported dataset-specific associations are (1) SMARCA4 loss is associated with markedly stronger SMARCA2 dependency, robust across global, adenocarcinoma, high screen quality, high Cas9 activity, low-growth, MYC-high, PTEN-loss, and ARID1A-loss contexts; (2) KEAP1 loss is associated with markedly weaker/less-negative NFE2L2 dependency, with discovery and independent validation concordant and robust across multiple contexts; (3) TP53 loss is associated with markedly weaker USP7 dependency, validated and reproducible in broad and several QC/biology-restricted contexts; (4) MSI-high is associated with markedly stronger WRN dependency, validated and robust including within high-quality, TP53-loss, and mutation-burden-selected settings; and (5) PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency, supported broadly, through multiple technical and biological contexts, and validated in high-IFN-gamma and high-EMT settings. H132 adds an independently validated high-EMT PTEN-loss/STAT3 context, albeit with attenuation relative to discovery.

Negative or unsupported findings include clinically meaningful null results for most direct receptor-tyrosine-kinase amplification effects on their own dependency scores: BRAF V600E did not support dependency_BRAF; EGFR amplification did not produce a robust self-dependency effect; ERBB2 amplification was near-null for dependency_ERBB2 and dependency_STAT3. MYC amplification did not support dependency_DHX9, dependency_RPL11, dependency_POLR2A, or dependency_KIF18A. Canonical TP53 loss did not show a stable clinically meaningful MDM2-dependency effect, and several technical QC-restricted follow-ups were null or small. RB1 loss remained unresolved for dependency_KIF18A, with near-zero or imprecise estimates. PTEN loss did not show a stable effect on dependency_KRAS among KRAS-mutant lines: the discovery-positive but validation-reversed H89 and the unresolved interaction H100 do not support a clinically meaningful KRAS-dependency modification. MSI-high had no supported effect on dependency_POLR2A after validation, and the constructed research markers D/E/F showed only small near-null associations.

The main unresolved uncertainty is whether several accepted context effects are context-specific or selected by the measured feature filters, especially in small exposed cells with strong screen-quality or expression-based eligibility filters. Multiplicity is substantial, and although validation intervals were wide because they accounted for the maximum number of validations, many accepted effects have very large lower bounds. The evidence establishes associations within this supplied dataset, not causality, therapeutic synthetic lethality, or generalizability outside these lung-line measurements.

Most informative next analyses are to evaluate the currently active claims that test accepted associations under additional high-Cas9 contexts: H170-H174 for PTEN-loss/STAT3 under high IFN, EMT, stemness, MYC, and AXL with high Cas9 activity; H155 for PTEN-loss/STAT3 under high-quality MYC-high screens; H180 for PTEN-loss/STAT3 under high serum with high Cas9; and H181 for KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 in slow-growing high-quality screens. If their signed lower bounds exceed the outcome-specific 10% benchmarks, they can add robustness or new accepted contexts; if lower bounds fall below benchmarks, the broader accepted effects should still stand but those narrower biological contexts should remain unresolved rather than accepted.

record.narrative: No assessments are due, so I make no status changes to existing claims. I registered twelve new comparisons to complement the currently active claims. Six are context-robustness tests for accepted dataset-specific associations: PTEN-loss-associated stronger dependency_STAT3 in low serum and high mutation burden; TP53-loss-associated weaker dependency_USP7 in high-quality interferon-high and EMT-high screens; SMARCA4-loss-associated stronger dependency_SMARCA2 in high-quality interferon-high and EMT-high screens; KEAP1-loss-associated weaker dependency_NFE2L2 in high-quality EMT-high and stemness-high screens; and MSI-high-associated stronger dependency_WRN in high-ploidy and high-interferon settings. For these, returned estimates are already signed to the registered direction, so positive signed estimates support the expected direction. Acceptance will require the signed lower bound to exceed an approximate 10% population-scale benchmark: about 0.028 for STAT3, 0.018 for USP7, 0.042 for SMARCA2, 0.009 for NFE2L2, and 0.030 for WRN. Plausible alternatives are context-specific attenuation, biological-state confounding, genomic-structure confounding, or selection by the measured feature filter. I also registered one new biology-driven hypothesis: CDKN2A loss in TP53-wildtype lines is hypothesized to be associated with stronger MDM2 dependency, potentially through disrupted p14ARF-MDM2-p53 regulation, with direction -1 and anticipated raw negative contrast; a null result is plausible because CDKN2A may not always reflect p14ARF, pathway redundancy may compensate, or MDM2 dependency may be driven by amplification rather than pathway state. The final proposal is a KEAP1-loss/lineage-subtype interaction for NFE2L2 dependency to assess whether the very strong accepted association differs between adenocarcinoma and the subtype complement; the anticipated value is near zero if generalizable within this lung-line dataset. No validation can be requested because voluntary validation budget is exhausted, so these remain discovery analyses in the supplied dataset and will not be treated as causal or generalizable beyond it.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

record.narrative: No assessments are currently due, so I make no status changes to existing claims. I request twelve previously registered, currently unevaluated active analyses. The selection is driven by two goals: (1) follow up the most informative active robustness questions identified in the previous synthesis, and (2) add diversity by testing new biology and one heterogeneity interaction. First, I request the PTEN-loss/dependency_STAT3 context tests H170-H174, H155, and H180. These ask whether the broadly accepted PTEN-loss/STAT3 association persists under additional biological and technical contexts: high IFN-gamma with high Cas9, high EMT with high Cas9, high stemness with high Cas9, high MYC with high Cas9, high AXL with high Cas9, high screen quality with high MYC, and high serum with high Cas9. For these direction -1 claims, returned estimates are already signed, so a positive signed lower bound supports the registered direction that PTEN loss is associated with stronger dependency_STAT3. I will require the signed lower bound to exceed an approximate 10% population-scale STAT3 benchmark of about 0.028 and interpret small exposed cells cautiously. Failure in one narrow context would not overturn the broad accepted association. Second, I request KEAP1-loss/dependency_NFE2L2 robustness in slow-growing high-quality screens H181 and EMT-high high-quality screens H188. These are direction +1 claims because KEAP1 loss has been associated with weaker/less-negative NFE2L2 dependency; positive signed evidence supports that direction. The approximate 10% population-scale benchmark for NFE2L2 is about 0.009, though effects in this system are very large, so acceptance should be clear if valid intervals are far above null. Third, I request WRN/MSI-high robustness under high ploidy H190. This tests whether the very strong MSI-high/WRN association persists when restricted to a genomically more unstable half of the population, which may help assess whether genomic structure confounds the main signal. Direction -1 means positive signed evidence supports stronger dependency_WRN in MSI-high lines; approximate benchmark about 0.030. Fourth, I request the new biology test H192: CDKN2A loss in TP53-wildtype lines associated with stronger dependency_MDM2. The mechanistic rationale is that CDKN2A/p14ARF status may alter MDM2-p53 pathway dependence even when TP53 is intact. Direction -1 means positive signed evidence supports stronger MDM2 dependency; approximate MDM2 benchmark about 0.027. A null or narrow interval near null is plausible given pathway redundancy and the fact that CDKN2A loss is not synonymous with p14ARF function. Finally, H193 tests whether the very strong KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 association differs between adenocarcinoma and the subtype complement within this lung-line dataset. The main effect is roughly 0.80, so I will treat only substantial heterogeneity, roughly 0.08-0.09 absolute or more, as scientifically meaningful; smaller estimates may indicate uncertainty or near-generalizability within the supplied data rather than decisive subtype-specificity. No validation can be requested because the voluntary validation budget is exhausted, so all results remain discovery associations within this supplied dataset.

I used the run's approximate 10% population-scale benchmarks: STAT3 about 0.028, NFE2L2 about 0.009, WRN about 0.030, and MDM2 about 0.027, while interpreting small exposed cells cautiously. H155, PTEN loss in high-quality MYC-high screens, had lower +0.047. MSI-high association with stronger dependency_WRN persisted in high-ploidy lines, H190 lower +0.728, accepted. CDKN2A loss in TP53-wildtype lines showed a clear clinically meaningful signed association with stronger dependency_MDM2, H192 lower +0.079, accepted; this is consistent with p14ARF-MDM2-p53 biology but remains observational and could reflect correlated genomic features. For H193, the KEAP1-loss/adenocarcinoma-subtype interaction for dependency_NFE2L2 was tiny and slightly negative, estimate -0.012, interval -0.057 to +0.033. The upper bound is far below the threshold I considered meaningful for heterogeneity of a main effect of about 0.80, so I reject the registered positive interaction and close it. All conclusions are associations within the supplied dataset, not evidence of causality, therapeutic dependency, or generalizability outside this dataset.

Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

Iteration 14/25, stage analyze, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score).
