Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link

Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.

is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).

If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.

For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: All returned estimates and intervals are signed to each claim's registered direction, so positive signed evidence supports the registered hypothesis. For the continuous dependency outcomes, I used the run's approximate 10% population-scale benchmarks while also checking absolute clinical magnitude and cell precision. PTEN loss showed clinically meaningful associations with stronger dependency_STAT3 in two additional contexts: low serum (H182, signed estimate +0.239, lower +0.163) and high mutation burden (H183, signed estimate +0.285, lower +0.188). These are accepted as dataset-specific context associations, not causal claims, and the effects are far above the STAT3 benchmark. TP53 loss showed robust signed evidence for the accepted weaker dependency_USP7 direction in high-quality inflammatory and EMT screens: H184 signed estimate +0.468 with lower +0.286, and H185 signed estimate +0.329 with lower +0.153. Both are well above the USP7 benchmark and are accepted. SMARCA4 loss continued to show very large signed associations with stronger dependency_SMARCA2 in high-quality IFN-high (H186, lower +0.705) and EMT-high screens (H187, lower +0.706); because the main effect is already very large, these tests function as robustness bounds and are accepted. MSI-high showed a very large signed association with stronger dependency_WRN in IFN-high lines (H191, signed estimate +0.825, lower +0.781), well above the WRN benchmark, and is accepted. CDKN2A loss in TP53-wildtype lines under high Cas9 showed a clinically meaningful signed association with stronger dependency_MDM2 (H194, signed estimate +0.141, lower +0.077), supporting the new pathway-relevant association under a screen-quality constraint. Notably, H196 tests CDKN2A loss within TP53-loss lines and also found a clinically meaningful positive signed effect (estimate +0.111, lower +0.035), which does not attenuate relative to the TP53-wildtype estimate in H192. Thus I accept H196 as evidence of a dataset-specific CDKN2A/MDM2 association in TP53-loss lines, but this weakens a simple p14ARF-MDM2-p53-context-only explanation and leaves open that the association may reflect correlated CDKN2A genomic features or other biology. H197 tested whether CDKN2A loss in TP53-wildtype lines also associates with weaker dependency_USP7; the signed estimate is essentially null and negative (-0.003), with a 95% interval from -0.025 to +0.020. The interval does not support the registered positive USP7 association and, given the wrong point estimate and the multiple-testing context, I reject the positive association while noting that a very small positive effect cannot be excluded. H198 tested adenocarcinoma-specific heterogeneity of the large SMARCA4/SMARCA2 association; the interaction is near null and signed negative (-0.028), with upper bound +0.020, below the SMARCA2 clinical-scale benchmark. This does not support the registered direction of stronger adenocarcinoma-specific enhancement, so I reject it. The lower bound could permit a modest opposite interaction, but that is not the registered claim and is not currently worth prioritization. H201 tested BRCA2 loss as a predictor of stronger dependency_DHX9; the signed estimate is positive but small (+0.012) and crosses null, with an upper bound that barely reaches the DHX9 benchmark. I leave it unresolved and deferred rather than accepting or closing, because the interval does not exclude a clinically meaningful positive effect, but the current evidence is weak and multiplicity is large. Voluntary validation budget is exhausted, so no validation request is made. All conclusions remain observational associations within the supplied dataset, not causal or generalizable claims.

The high-ploidy CDKN2A/MDM2 claim tests whether the association is robust to genome instability or plausibly driven by co-occurring copy-number features. The low-Cas9 claims are technical robustness checks for accepted core associations: if effects remain clinically meaningful at lower Cas9 activity, the associations are less likely to require highly potent screens; if they attenuate, that indicates screen-potency sensitivity rather than refuting the broader accepted effects. I set H201 active because it remains weak and unresolved and the new high-TMB refinement is more biologically targeted. All results remain observational associations within this dataset, not causal or therapeutic claims; validation budget is exhausted.

results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

record.narrative:
All returned estimates and intervals are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction, so a positive signed estimate supports the registered claim and a negative signed estimate opposes it. For the -1 claims, this corresponds to the more-negative dependency-score direction being stronger in the exposed group. I used the run-level approximate 10% population-scale benchmarks, while also checking absolute magnitude, cell precision, and the pre-registered context. Validation budget is exhausted, so no validation was requested and the new evidence cannot be externally confirmed within this run.

MDM2/CDKN2A follow-up: H195 is accepted. In TP53-wildtype lines with high screen ROC quality, CDKN2A loss shows a clinically meaningful association with stronger dependency_MDM2, signed estimate +0.142 with lower bound +0.084, well above the approximate MDM2 benchmark near 0.027. This supports robustness under screen-quality restriction. H209 is accepted. Within MTAP-intact lines, CDKN2A loss remains associated with stronger dependency_MDM2, signed estimate +0.105 with lower bound +0.067. This is scientifically useful for specificity: it reduces concern that the CDKN2A/MDM2 signal is purely an MTAP or 9p21 co-deletion artifact, because the association persists when MTAP loss is excluded. H208 is left unresolved and closed. MTAP loss alone has a small positive signed estimate +0.019 and a 95% interval from -0.008 to +0.045. The point is below the approximate MDM2 clinical benchmark and crosses null, but the interval does not exclude a clinically meaningful positive effect, so I do not reject it decisively. H207 is also left unresolved and closed. The TP53-loss interaction for CDKN2A/MDM2 is near zero, signed estimate +0.008, interval -0.077 to +0.093. This does not support strong p53-context heterogeneity, but the interval is wide and includes clinically meaningful positive heterogeneity, so the best conclusion is that the current evidence is too imprecise to establish or exclude a modifier effect. Taken with accepted H192 and H196, the MDM2/CDKN2A association is not strictly a p53-context-only finding in this dataset, but causal mechanisms remain uncertain.

SMARCA2/MYC context: H199 is unresolved and closed. In SMARCA4-loss lines, MYC amplification has a small positive signed estimate +0.023, interval -0.030 to +0.077, with a small exposed cell n=59. The interval cannot exclude a clinically meaningful positive effect, but it does not provide sufficient evidence to accept a clinically meaningful MYC amplification effect on dependency_SMARCA2. H200 is rejected. In SMARCA4-intact lines, the signed estimate for MYC amplification and stronger dependency_SMARCA2 is -0.012, interval -0.037 to +0.014. The point estimate opposes the registered direction, and the positive upper bound is well below the SMARCA2 benchmark near 0.042, so there is no evidence for a clinically meaningful positive effect of MYC amplification on dependency_SMARCA2 in SMARCA4-intact lines. This is a negative specificity result for MYC-amplification modification of the SMARCA4/SMARCA2 association.

Large-effect modifier checks: H202 and H203 are left unresolved and closed. For MSI-high/WRN, the TP53-loss interaction has signed estimate +0.053, interval -0.022 to +0.127; the point exceeds the approximate WRN benchmark, but the exposed cell count is very small and the interval crosses null. For KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2, the TP53-loss interaction has signed estimate +0.018, interval -0.034 to +0.069. These tests show lack of clear p53-context heterogeneity for the main effects, but because the main effects are very large and the interaction CIs are wide, they should not be interpreted as proof that p53 status has no modifier effect. Closing them reflects that these one-off context tests have not produced decisive evidence and no independent validation budget remains.

Genomic and screen-context robustness: H189 is accepted. KEAP1 loss remains associated with weaker dependency_NFE2L2, signed estimate +0.773, lower bound +0.719, in high-screen-quality high-stemness lines. This is far above the NFE2L2 benchmark and extends accepted KEAP1/NFE2L2 robustness. H204 is accepted. PTEN loss remains associated with stronger dependency_STAT3 in higher-ploidy lines, signed estimate +0.294, lower bound +0.218, far above the STAT3 benchmark. H205 is accepted. TP53 loss remains associated with weaker dependency_USP7 in higher-ploidy lines, signed estimate +0.330, lower bound +0.225, far above the USP7 benchmark. These acceptances support robustness of accepted core associations across genome-instability contexts, but remain observational dataset-specific associations.

New DHX9/RB1 finding: H206 is rejected as registered. The original hypothesis was RB1 loss associated with stronger, more negative dependency_DHX9, direction -1. The signed estimate is -0.035 with interval -0.061 to -0.009. In signed terms this opposes the registered direction; in raw terms it indicates RB1-loss lines have a less negative dependency_DHX9 score than RB1-intact lines, i.e. weaker measured DHX9 dependency. The magnitude is near the approximate DHX9 benchmark and the signed interval excludes null for the opposite direction. However, because this direction was not pre-registered and many context tests have been performed, I registered H216 as an exploratory reversal with parent H206 and motivating evidence R192. H216 is unresolved and should be treated as hypothesis-generating rather than confirmatory. Competing explanations remain, including confounding by cell-cycle or screen-related biology in RB1-loss lines, copy-number correlates, and multiplicity.

Audit: The eligibility filters are pre-specified and not outcome-derived, so outcome leakage is unlikely in the requested contrasts. The main risk is multiplicity across many genomic, technical, and phenotype contexts, especially for interactions and small-cell filters. I therefore required large intervals excluding null and exceeding clinical-scale benchmarks before accepting. Interactions were interpreted conservatively: near-null point estimates are lack of evidence for a specific modifier, not proof of homogeneity unless the interval excludes clinically meaningful heterogeneity. H209 partially addresses locus-level confounding for CDKN2A/MDM2 by excluding MTAP loss. H206 shows the value of pre-registering direction, because the observed effect is opposite and would otherwise invite selective interpretation. All conclusions are limited to associations in this supplied dataset and do not imply causality, therapeutic vulnerability, or generalizability.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.

comparison cell.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.

request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released

the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.

For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

Because validation budget is exhausted, these are discovery-only analyses within the supplied dataset and are not causal or generalizability claims.","appraise":"All returned estimates and intervals are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction, so a positive signed estimate supports the registered claim and a negative signed estimate opposes it. For the -1 claims, this corresponds to the more-negative dependency-score direction being stronger in the exposed group. I used the run-level approximate 10% population-scale benchmarks, while also checking absolute magnitude, cell precision, and the pre-registered context. Validation budget is exhausted, so no validation was requested and the new evidence cannot be externally confirmed within this run.\n\nMDM2/CDKN2A follow-up: H195 is accepted. In TP53-wildtype lines with high screen ROC quality, CDKN2A loss shows a clinically meaningful association with stronger dependency_MDM2, signed estimate +0.142 with lower bound +0.084, well above the approximate MDM2 benchmark near 0.027. This supports robustness under screen-quality restriction. H209 is accepted. Within MTAP-intact lines, CDKN2A loss remains associated with stronger dependency_MDM2, signed estimate +0.105 with lower bound +0.067. This is scientifically useful for specificity: it reduces concern that the CDKN2A/MDM2 signal is purely an MTAP or 9p21 co-deletion artifact, because the association persists when MTAP loss is excluded. H208 is left unresolved and closed. MTAP loss alone has a small positive signed estimate +0.019 and a 95% interval from -0.008 to +0.045. The point is below the approximate MDM2 clinical benchmark and crosses null, but the interval does not exclude a clinically meaningful positive effect, so I do not reject it decisively. H207 is also left unresolved and closed. The TP53-loss interaction for CDKN2A/MDM2 is near zero, signed estimate +0.008, interval -0.077 to +0.093. This does not support strong p53-context heterogeneity, but the interval is wide and includes clinically meaningful positive heterogeneity, so the best conclusion is that the current evidence is too imprecise to establish or exclude a modifier effect. Taken with accepted H192 and H196, the MDM2/CDKN2A association is not strictly a p53-context-only finding in this dataset, but causal mechanisms remain uncertain.\n\nSMARCA2/MYC context: H199 is unresolved and closed. In SMARCA4-loss lines, MYC amplification has a small positive signed estimate +0.023, interval -0.030 to +0.077, with a small exposed cell n=59. The interval cannot exclude a clinically meaningful positive effect, but it does not provide sufficient evidence to accept a clinically meaningful MYC amplification effect on dependency_SMARCA2. H200 is rejected. In SMARCA4-intact lines, the signed estimate for MYC amplification and stronger dependency_SMARCA2 is -0.012, interval -0.037 to +0.014. The point estimate opposes the registered direction, and the positive upper bound is well below the SMARCA2 benchmark near 0.042, so there is no evidence for a clinically meaningful positive effect of MYC amplification on dependency_SMARCA2 in SMARCA4-intact lines. This is a negative specificity result for MYC-amplification modification of the SMARCA4/SMARCA2 association.\n\nLarge-effect modifier checks: H202 and H203 are left unresolved and closed. For MSI-high/WRN, the TP53-loss interaction has signed estimate +0.053, interval -0.022 to +0.127; the point exceeds the approximate WRN benchmark, but the exposed cell count is very small and the interval crosses null. For KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2, the TP53-loss interaction has signed estimate +0.018, interval -0.034 to +0.069. These tests show lack of clear p53-context heterogeneity for the main effects, but because the main effects are very large and the interaction CIs are wide, they should not be interpreted as proof that p53 status has no modifier effect. Closing them reflects that these one-off context tests have not produced decisive evidence and no independent validation budget remains.\n\nGenomic and screen-context robustness: H189 is accepted. KEAP1 loss remains associated with weaker dependency_NFE2L2, signed estimate +0.773, lower bound +0.719, in high-screen-quality high-stemness lines. This is far above the NFE2L2 benchmark and extends accepted KEAP1/NFE2L2 robustness. H204 is accepted. PTEN loss remains associated with stronger dependency_STAT3 in higher-ploidy lines, signed estimate +0.294, lower bound +0.218, far above the STAT3 benchmark. H205 is accepted. TP53 loss remains associated with weaker dependency_USP7 in higher-ploidy lines, signed estimate +0.330, lower bound +0.225, far above the USP7 benchmark. These acceptances support robustness of accepted core associations across genome-instability contexts, but remain observational dataset-specific associations.\n\nNew DHX9/RB1 finding: H206 is rejected as registered. The original hypothesis was RB1 loss associated with stronger, more negative dependency_DHX9, direction -1. The signed estimate is -0.035 with interval -0.061 to -0.009. In signed terms this opposes the registered direction; in raw terms it indicates RB1-loss lines have a less negative dependency_DHX9 score than RB1-intact lines, i.e. weaker measured DHX9 dependency. The magnitude is near the approximate DHX9 benchmark and the signed interval excludes null for the opposite direction. However, because this direction was not pre-registered and many context tests have been performed, I registered H216 as an exploratory reversal with parent H206 and motivating evidence R192. H216 is unresolved and should be treated as hypothesis-generating rather than confirmatory. Competing explanations remain, including confounding by cell-cycle or screen-related biology in RB1-loss lines, copy-number correlates, and multiplicity.\n\nAudit: The eligibility filters are pre-specified and not outcome-derived, so outcome leakage is unlikely in the requested contrasts. The main risk is multiplicity across many genomic, technical, and phenotype contexts, especially for interactions and small-cell filters. I therefore required large intervals excluding null and exceeding clinical-scale benchmarks before accepting. Interactions were interpreted conservatively: near-null point estimates are lack of evidence for a specific modifier, not proof of homogeneity unless the interval excludes clinically meaningful heterogeneity. H209 partially addresses locus-level confounding for CDKN2A/MDM2 by excluding MTAP loss. H206 shows the value of pre-registering direction, because the observed effect is opposite and would otherwise invite selective interpretation. All conclusions are limited to associations in this supplied dataset and do not imply causality, therapeutic vulnerability, or generalizability.","synthesize":"No assessment_due was delivered and no new validation evidence arrived in this synthesis turn. Representative accepted claims include H192, H194, and H196. record.narrative: No new validation evidence or response deadline was delivered, and the voluntary validation budget is exhausted. I therefore made no status changes for existing claims; the accepted scientific conclusions from the prior synthesis remain current. The strongest dataset-specific findings are stable associations, not causal or therapeutic claims. First, SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger dependency_SMARCA2, meaning a more negative dependency score, with very large signed effects across global, lineage, screen-quality, Cas9-quality, ploidy, EMT, PTEN-loss, ARID1A-loss, slow-growth, and many other contexts. Second, KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker dependency_NFE2L2, meaning a less negative score, validated and reproduced broadly. Third, TP53 loss is associated with weaker dependency_USP7, validated and stable in many quality-controlled and biologically defined contexts. Fourth, MSI-high status is associated with markedly stronger dependency_WRN, validated and robust across several screen-quality and genomic contexts. Fifth, PTEN loss is associated with stronger dependency_STAT3, with several validated and broadly supported context-specific acceptances. Sixth, CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger dependency_MDM2, with clinically meaningful effects in TP53-wildtype, high-Cas9, high-screen-quality, TP53-loss, MTAP-intact, and high-ploidy-robust contexts; the MTAP-intact persistence reduces concern that this is purely an MTAP or 9p21 co-deletion artifact, though mechanisms remain unproven. Negative or unsupported findings include direct receptor self-dependencies: BRAF V600E did not support dependency_BRAF, EGFR amplification was not accepted as a stable dependency_EGFR effect, and ERBB2 amplification was near-null or not accepted for dependency_ERBB2 and tested STAT3 contrasts. KRAS mutation was not a stable predictor of dependency_KRAS or dependency_RIT1. Canonical TP53 loss did not robustly predict dependency_MDM2, and MYC amplification did not support dependency_DHX9, dependency_RPL11, dependency_POLR2A, dependency_KIF18A, or the tested dependency_MDM2 context. MSI-high did not support dependency_POLR2A after validation. PTEN loss did not robustly modify dependency_KRAS among KRAS-mutant lines. CDKN2A loss did not support the tested USP7 direction. Constructed markers D/E/F remain uninformative for dependency_STAT3. record.narrative: No assessments are due, so I leave existing claims unchanged and propose targeted refinements that add technical robustness, locus specificity, and boundary-condition checks for already-supported or hypothesis-generating findings. The two low-Cas9 proposals test whether accepted PTEN-loss/dependency_STAT3 and CDKN2A-loss/dependency_MDM2 associations persist when screen potency is lower; persistence would reduce concern that these associations are only detectable in highly potent screens, while attenuation would indicate screen-potency sensitivity without refuting the broader accepted effects. The MTAP-loss interaction tests whether the CDKN2A/dependency_MDM2 association is amplified in MTAP-deleted lines, refining the earlier MTAP-intact result that argued against a pure 9p21/MTAP co-deletion artifact. The RB1-loss/dependency_DHX9 proposal follows the exploratory reversal from H206/H216 and asks whether the weaker measured DHX9 dependency persists in high-screen-quality, MYC-amplification-negative lines. The low-ploidy MSI-high/dependency_WRN test adds a genome-instability boundary condition for an already very strong accepted association. The BRCA2-loss/dependency_DHX9 refinement under high mutation burden and high screen quality is a stricter replication-stress test than the weak global BRCA2/DHX9 result. For signed estimates, a positive signed mean difference supports the registered direction: for direction -1 it corresponds to a more negative dependency score in the exposed group, whereas for direction +1 it corresponds to a less negative, weaker dependency score in the exposed group. Approximate 10% population-scale benchmarks remain about 0.027 for MDM2, 0.018 for USP7, 0.042 for SMARCA2, 0.009 for NFE2L2, 0.030 for DHX9, 0.028 for STAT3, and 0.030 for WRN. record.narrative: No claims are due for assessment, so I do not change existing statuses. I request analyses for 12 existing active comparisons that currently have no direct result in the ledger. The selection serves three scientific purposes. First, it tests whether accepted core associations are robust to reduced CRISPR potency: H213 (TP53 loss with weaker USP7), H214 (SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2), H215 (KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2), and H222 (CDKN2A loss with stronger MDM2). If their signed lower bounds remain above clinically relevant magnitude in low-Cas9 strata, the associations are less likely to be artifacts of very potent screens; if they attenuate, the effects may be potency-sensitive. Second, it tests genome-instability boundaries for accepted and emerging effects: H210/H217 for CDKN2A/MDM2 in high- and low-ploidy lines, H218 for PTEN/STAT3 in low ploidy, H219 for TP53/USP7 in low ploidy, and H225 for MSI-high/WRN in low ploidy. Third, it refines two emerging areas: H223 tests whether the CDKN2A-loss/dependency_MDM2 association is stronger in MTAP-loss lines versus its complement, adding specificity evidence beyond the accepted MTAP-intact result; and the DHX9 panel H212 and H224 tests replication-stress biology and the exploratory opposite-direction RB1-loss signal. These are all previously registered comparisons and, except for context refinements, are not being run again to recycle prior evidence. The controller will perform Welch independent-cell comparisons with 95% intervals and cell-count eligibility. Estimates and intervals will be interpreted as already signed to the claim direction. I will accept only when the point estimate is clinically meaningful and the interval supports the direction with reasonable precision; unresolved when intervals are wide or cross meaningful scales; and reject when the signed point and interval oppose the registered direction or exclude a meaningful positive effect. Because validation budget is exhausted, any acceptances remain observations of association in this supplied dataset, not causal or generalizable claims.

H215 is accepted for KEAP1 loss with weaker dependency_NFE2L2 in low-Cas9 lines; signed estimate 0.7994, lower 0.7513, far above the NFE2L2 benchmark. H222 is accepted for CDKN2A loss with stronger dependency_MDM2 in low-Cas9 lines; signed estimate 0.1088, lower 0.0458, above the MDM2 benchmark. These acceptances support the robustness of accepted core associations under reduced CRISPR screen potency. Ploidy boundary conditions: H210 is accepted in high-ploidy lines, CDKN2A loss with stronger dependency_MDM2; signed estimate 0.1073, lower 0.0600, above benchmark. H217 is accepted in low-ploidy lines; signed estimate 0.1167, lower 0.0419, above benchmark. expectation

evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative: No new validation result was delivered in this synthesis and no original-claim response deadline was open, so no accept/reject/unresolved scientific status is changed here. The voluntary validation budget is exhausted, so all conclusions remain dataset-specific associations rather than causal, therapeutic, or generalizable claims. The final scientific report is: six main measured predictors/subgroups are supported as clinically meaningful associations in this supplied dataset. First, SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger dependency_SMARCA2, meaning more negative dependency scores in SMARCA4-loss lines, with very large signed effects and repeated acceptances across global, lineage, screen-quality, Cas9-quality, ploidy, EMT, PTEN-loss, ARID1A-loss, MYC-expression, slow-growth, IFN, and other contexts; the H31 validation result strongly supports this. Second, KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker dependency_NFE2L2, meaning less negative dependency scores in KEAP1-loss lines, with validated and broad context-specific reproduction. Third, TP53 loss is associated with weaker dependency_USP7, meaning less negative USP7 dependency scores in TP53-loss lines, with validation and many robust context acceptances. Fourth, MSI-high status is associated with markedly stronger dependency_WRN, with validation and broad reproduction across screen quality, mutation burden, ploidy, IFN, TP53-loss, and low-Cas9 contexts. Fifth, PTEN loss is associated with stronger dependency_STAT3, with multiple validations and broad acceptances across quality, Cas9 potency, ploidy, EMT, IFN, stemness, mutation burden, and expression contexts. Sixth, CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger dependency_MDM2, with clinically meaningful effects in TP53-wildtype, TP53-loss, MTAP-intact, high-Cas9, low-Cas9, high-screen-quality, and both high- and low-ploidy contexts; MTAP-intact persistence and the unresolved MTAP interaction reduce concern that this is purely an MTAP or 9p21 co-deletion artifact, but mechanism remains unproven. Negative or unsupported findings include direct receptor self-dependencies and several canonical expectations: BRAF V600E did not support dependency_BRAF, EGFR amplification was not accepted as a stable dependency_EGFR effect and validation remained imprecise, ERBB2 amplification was near-null for dependency_ERBB2 and tested STAT3 contrasts, KRAS mutation was not a stable predictor of dependency_KRAS or dependency_RIT1, and MYC amplification did not support dependency_DHX9, dependency_RPL11, dependency_POLR2A, dependency_KIF18A, or the tested dependency_MDM2 context. Canonical TP53 loss did not robustly predict dependency_MDM2, MSI-high did not support dependency_POLR2A after validation, PTEN loss did not robustly modify dependency_KRAS among KRAS-mutant lines after validation, and CDKN2A loss did not support the tested dependency_USP7 direction. Constructed markers D/E/F remain uninformative for dependency_STAT3. Unresolved uncertainty remains for EGFR amplification because the discovery point was positive but imprecise and validation did not resolve it; for the CDKN2A/MTAP interaction on dependency_MDM2; and for the DHX9 panel, where original RB1-loss strong-DHX9 was rejected, the reversed weaker-DHX9 signal is exploratory, BRCA2-loss effects are weak, and MSI-high and stricter BRCA2/RB1-context tests remain unresolved. Interaction near-nulls, especially for very large main effects, should be read as insufficient evidence for a tested modifier rather than proof of homogeneity. The most informative next analysis is H211, testing MSI-high versus non-MSI-high dependency_DHX9 under high screen quality and high Cas9 activity, because it can distinguish whether MSI biology affects DHX9 beyond the very strong WRN association or whether MSI effects are WRN-specific. H226, the strict BRCA2-loss DHX9 test under high mutation burden and high screen quality, is the next highest-priority active test. H224 remains relevant for specificity of the exploratory RB1-loss weaker-DHX9 signal in high-quality, MYC-amplification-negative lines. H201 and H216 are closed as low-priority unresolved exploratory leads, and H212 and H220 are deferred in favor of the stricter H226 and focused H224/H211 analysis.

Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

record.narrative: All estimates and intervals are interpreted as already signed to the registered hypothesis direction. For direction -1, a positive signed estimate means more negative dependency score in exposed cells, i.e. stronger dependency; for direction +1, a positive signed estimate means less negative dependency score, i.e. weaker dependency. I judged these results against the approximate 10%-of-mean clinical-scale benchmarks used throughout this run: about 0.042 for SMARCA2, 0.030 for WRN, 0.025-0.030 for DHX9, 0.028 for STAT3, 0.027 for MDM2, 0.018 for USP7, and 0.009 for NFE2L2. Acceptance required a clear clinically meaningful point estimate and an interval that reasonably excludes null and, for new or context-specific claims, reasonably supports a clinically meaningful rather than merely statistically distinguishable effect. H229 through H234 are a strong technical robustness block: in Avana-library lines with high screen discrimination, the six core accepted associations persist with very large signed effects and adequate exposed-cell counts. SMARCA4 loss remains strongly associated with stronger dependency_SMARCA2 (0.794, 0.767 to 0.820); TP53 loss with weaker dependency_USP7 (0.441, 0.351 to 0.530); KEAP1 loss with weaker dependency_NFE2L2 (0.793, 0.764 to 0.821); MSI-high with stronger dependency_WRN (0.797, 0.759 to 0.834); PTEN loss with stronger dependency_STAT3 (0.254, 0.184 to 0.324); and CDKN2A loss with stronger dependency_MDM2 (0.133, 0.082 to 0.184). These intervals lie far above the relevant clinical-scale benchmarks, so I accept them as dataset-specific robustness findings and close the investigations. H45 and H46 are reciprocal specificity checks rather than mere repetitions. The TP53-loss association with weaker USP7 persists when KEAP1 loss is absent (0.370, 0.289 to 0.452), and the KEAP1-loss association with weaker NFE2L2 persists when TP53 loss is absent (0.792, 0.770 to 0.815). Both are accepted and closed as evidence against a simple co-alteration artifact for the tested pairing, though they still do not establish mechanism or causality. H227 is the closest boundary case. CDKN2A loss in high mutation-burden lines gives a very large positive signed estimate (0.095) and the interval excludes null (0.024 to 0.167), but the lower bound is slightly below the 0.027 MDM2 benchmark. I therefore do not accept this specific high-mutation-burden context as decisive under the 10% clinical-scale criterion; I keep it unresolved and active and registered a stricter high-mutation-burden plus high-screen-quality refinement to test whether precision and effect size can move the lower bound above the benchmark. H211 and H226 are strict negative or inconclusive DHX9 tests. MSI-high dependency_DHX9 under high screen quality and high Cas9 activity is tiny and imprecise (0.008, -0.049 to 0.064), and BRCA2-loss dependency_DHX9 under high mutation burden and high screen quality is similarly weak and imprecise (0.011, -0.046 to 0.069). These do not support clinically meaningful DHX9 associations in the tested contexts; I close them. H228 tests whether the PTEN-loss effect on dependency_STAT3 differs by KRAS-mutant status. The signed interaction is negative (-0.024), opposite the registered direction, with a wide interval (-0.148 to 0.100). It does not support the hypothesized modification, but it is too imprecise to establish absence of modification. I keep it unresolved and closed as a low-priority interaction question. From an audit standpoint, all eligibility filters were specified from predictor, technical, or phenotype variables rather than outcome-derived selection, so outcome leakage is unlikely. The dominant risks are multiplicity, small-cell subgroup instability, and overinterpreting near-benchmark context effects. I accepted only very large, well-powered robustness and specificity results; near-benchmark, wide, or low-CI results remain unresolved. With validation budget exhausted, every acceptance remains an internal association in the supplied dataset, not a causal, therapeutic, or externally generalizable claim.

Acceptance required a meaningful point estimate and an interval that reasonably excludes null and a clinically meaningful opposite effect. Supported main findings:
1. SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger dependency_SMARCA2. This is the strongest and most repeatedly supported result. Direction -1 acceptances mean SMARCA4-loss lines have more negative SMARCA2 dependency. Effects are approximately 0.75-0.82, far above the 0.042 benchmark, with independent validation support in H31/R40 and broad robustness across lineage, screen quality, Cas9 activity, ploidy, IFN, EMT, slow growth, MYC expression, PTEN loss, and ARID1A-loss contexts. Direction +1 acceptances mean KEAP1-loss lines have less negative NFE2L2 dependency. Effects are approximately 0.77-0.81, far above the 0.009 benchmark, with robustness in adenocarcinoma, high screen quality, high Cas9, low Cas9, ploidy, IFN, EMT, stemness, PTEN-loss, and TP53-loss or TP53-intact contexts. H46/R217 supports the result among TP53-intact lines, arguing against a simple KEAP1/TP53 co-alteration explanation for the tested pairing. Mechanism still cannot be inferred from association alone.
3. TP53 loss is associated with weaker dependency_USP7. Direction +1 acceptances mean TP53-loss lines have less negative USP7 dependency. Effects are approximately 0.37-0.45, well above the 0.018 benchmark, with independent validation in H8/R39 and additional validated or robust contexts including H112/R92 and R93 among KEAP1-loss lines and H45/R216 among KEAP1-intact lines. The association persists across high and low Cas9, high screen quality, ploidy, AXL high expression, MYC high expression, IFN, EMT, Avana library, and multiple exclusion contexts. Again, this is an association in this dataset, not a causal TP53 effect.
4. MSI-high status is associated with markedly stronger dependency_WRN. Direction -1 acceptances mean MSI-high lines have more negative WRN dependency. Effects are approximately 0.77-0.83, far above the 0.030 benchmark, with independent validation in H9/R53 and broad reproduction in high mutation burden, high and low ploidy, IFN, TP53-loss, low Cas9, high screen quality, and Avana high-ROC contexts. This is a very strong dataset-specific association. The tested MSI effect on dependency_POLR2A was not supported after validation, so MSI association appears WRN-specific among the tested outcomes.
5. PTEN loss is associated with stronger dependency_STAT3. Direction -1 acceptances mean PTEN-loss lines have more negative STAT3 dependency. Effects are approximately 0.19-0.37, above the 0.028 benchmark, with multiple independent validation supports including H80/R66, H109/R107, H113/R106, H112/R93 is USP7 not STAT3, H123/R120, and H132/R133. Interaction tests for PTEN loss on dependency_STAT3 were mostly wide or inconsistent; they do not establish a reliable modifier, despite the robust main association.
6. CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger dependency_MDM2. Direction -1 acceptances mean CDKN2A-loss lines have more negative MDM2 dependency. This association has not been independently validated because validation budget is exhausted, but it is internally replicated across many technical and genomic contexts. H209/R185 in MTAP-intact lines reduces concern that the effect is purely an MTAP or 9p21 co-deletion surrogate, though MTAP interaction remains unresolved and mechanism remains unproven.

Negative or unsupported findings: canonical receptor self-dependency and several pathway expectations were not supported. BRAF V600E did not support stronger dependency_BRAF. EGFR amplification was not accepted as a stable clinically meaningful dependency_EGFR effect, and validation remained imprecise. ERBB2 amplification was near null for dependency_ERBB2 and did not support tested dependency_STAT3 contrasts. KRAS mutation was not a stable predictor of stronger dependency_KRAS and did not support dependency_RIT1. MYC amplification did not support dependency_DHX9, dependency_RPL11, dependency_POLR2A, or dependency_KIF18A. RB1 loss did not support stronger dependency_DHX9; H206/R192 was rejected because the signed estimate opposed the stronger-dependency hypothesis. Canonical TP53 loss did not robustly predict dependency_MDM2. MSI-high did not support dependency_POLR2A after validation. PTEN loss did not robustly modify dependency_KRAS among KRAS-mutant lines after validation. CDKN2A loss did not support the tested dependency_USP7 direction. Constructed research markers D, E, and F were uninformative for dependency_STAT3 and related outcomes where tested.

Unresolved uncertainty: EGFR amplification remains unresolved because discovery was positive but imprecise and validation did not resolve the interval. KRAS mutation and NF1-loss effects on dependency_KRAS remain unresolved or low-priority because effects are small, directionally unstable, or imprecise. The dependency_DHX9 panel remains the least resolved area: the original stronger-DHX9 RB1 hypothesis was rejected, the reversed weaker-DHX9 signal is exploratory, MSI and BRCA2-loss contexts were weak or closed, and H224/R205 remains active but near benchmark; H236 is a registered stricter technical refinement. CDKN2A loss on dependency_MDM2 in high mutation burden remains unresolved because H227/R208 has a large point estimate but a lower confidence limit slightly below the 0.027 benchmark; H235 is registered to address this. Interaction and subgroup near-nulls for accepted large main effects, especially PTEN/STAT3, KEAP1/NFE2L2, TP53/USP7, SMARCA4/SMARCA2, MSI/WRN, and CDKN2A/MTAP/MDM2, generally indicate insufficient evidence for a tested modifier rather than proof of homogeneity. Because validation budget is exhausted and all analyses are from one dataset, none of the accepted associations can be interpreted as causal or generallyizable without external replication.

This directly addresses the closest boundary between supported and unresolved for an accepted core association: H227 has a large positive signed effect but a lower bound just below the clinical-scale benchmark. H46/R217 supports the result among TP53-intact lines, arguing against a simple KEAP1/TP53 co-alteration explanation for the tested pairing. Mechanism still cannot be inferred from association alone.
3. TP53 loss is associated with weaker dependency_USP7. Direction +1 acceptances mean TP53-loss lines have less negative USP7 dependency. Effects are approximately 0.37-0.45, well above the 0.018 benchmark, with independent validation in H8/R39 and additional validated or robust contexts including H112/R92 and R93 among KEAP1-loss lines and H45/R216 among KEAP1-intact lines. The association persists across high and low Cas9, high screen quality, ploidy, AXL high expression, MYC high expression, IFN, EMT, Avana library, and multiple exclusion contexts. 4. MSI-high status is associated with markedly stronger dependency_WRN. Direction -1 acceptances mean MSI-high lines have more negative WRN dependency. Effects are approximately 0.77-0.83, far above the 0.030 benchmark, with independent validation in H9/R53 and broad reproduction in high mutation burden, high and low ploidy, IFN, TP53-loss, low Cas9, high screen quality, and Avana high-ROC contexts. Effects are approximately 0.19-0.37, above the 0.028 benchmark, with multiple independent validation supports including H80/R66, H109/R107, H113/R106, H112/R93 is USP7 not STAT3, H123/R120, and H132/R133. Returned estimates are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction, so I interpret signed positive values as supporting the registered hypothesis and signed negative values as opposing it. Because dependency outcomes can be negative, I used approximate 10%-of-absolute-population-mean clinical-scale benchmarks: roughly 0.042 for dependency_SMARCA2, 0.030 for dependency_WRN, 0.030 conservative for dependency_DHX9, 0.028 for dependency_STAT3, 0.027 for dependency_MDM2, 0.018 for dependency_USP7, and 0.009 for dependency_NFE2L2. Acceptance required a meaningful point estimate and an interval that reasonably excludes null and a clinically meaningful opposite effect. All conclusions are dataset-specific associations, not causal, therapeutic, or externally generalizable claims.\n\nSupported main findings:\n1. SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger dependency_SMARCA2. This is the strongest and most repeatedly supported result. Direction -1 acceptances mean SMARCA4-loss lines have more negative SMARCA2 dependency. Effects are approximately 0.75-0.82, far above the 0.042 benchmark, with independent validation support in H31/R40 and broad robustness across lineage, screen quality, Cas9 activity, ploidy, IFN, EMT, slow growth, MYC expression, PTEN loss, and ARID1A-loss contexts. Reciprocal specificity is also useful: ARID1A loss among SMARCA4-intact lines was rejected for dependency_SMARCA2 in H43/R37, reducing support for a simple ARID1A/9p21 co-deletion artifact, while SMARCA4 effects persist in many exclusion contexts.\n2. KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker dependency_NFE2L2. This was established by the reversal and validation in H22/R6 and R26. Direction +1 acceptances mean KEAP1-loss lines have less negative NFE2L2 dependency. Effects are approximately 0.77-0.81, far above the 0.009 benchmark, with robustness in adenocarcinoma, high screen quality, high Cas9, low Cas9, ploidy, IFN, EMT, stemness, PTEN-loss, and TP53-loss or TP53-intact contexts. H46/R217 supports the result among TP53-intact lines, arguing against a simple KEAP1/TP53 co-alteration explanation for the tested pairing. Mechanism still cannot be inferred from association alone.\n3. TP53 loss is associated with weaker dependency_USP7. Direction +1 acceptances mean TP53-loss lines have less negative USP7 dependency. Effects are approximately 0.37-0.45, well above the 0.018 benchmark, with independent validation in H8/R39 and additional validated or robust contexts including H112/R92 and R93 among KEAP1-loss lines and H45/R216 among KEAP1-intact lines. The association persists across high and low Cas9, high screen quality, ploidy, AXL high expression, MYC high expression, IFN, EMT, Avana library, and multiple exclusion contexts. Again, this is an association in this dataset, not a causal TP53 effect.\n4. MSI-high status is associated with markedly stronger dependency_WRN. evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

Iteration 19/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
