The final synthesis therefore relies on the controller-maintained accepted set and treats all results as associations within the supplied lung-lineage CRISPR dataset, not as causal, therapeutic, or externally generalizable claims. For practical significance, I used a roughly 10 percent benchmark relative to the relevant absolute mean dependency score; because these scores are negative and centered near about -0.2 to -0.4, this corresponds roughly to 0.02 to 0.03 units for most outcomes and about 0.04 units for SMARCA2. This is a heuristic, not a formal equivalence test.\n\nSupported dataset-specific associations. First, SMARCA4 loss is associated with markedly stronger SMARCA2 dependency. Accepted contrasts are about 0.76 to 0.82 dependency-score units more negative in SMARCA4-loss lines than in SMARCA4-intact lines, far above the practical benchmark, and the pattern is reproduced across adenocarcinoma, library, screen-quality, Cas9-activity, proliferation, expression, ploidy, and ARID1A contexts. Representative strata such as H31 have independent validation, so this is a robust internal synthetic-lethal-like association rather than an external causal claim.\n\nSecond, KEAP1 loss is associated with markedly weaker NFE2L2 dependency. Accepted contrasts are about 0.78 to 0.81 units less negative in KEAP1-loss lines, with independent validation of the main reverse-direction claim and clean-background confirmation. This is a large and stable dataset-specific association.\n\nThird, TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency. Accepted contrasts are about 0.32 to 0.51 units less negative, above the USP7 benchmark, and internally robust across lineage, library, screen quality, Cas9 activity, co-mutation, ploidy, growth-rate, and expression strata. Overall TP53-loss/USP7 and some contexts received independent validation. The same TP53-loss exposure did not produce a comparable robust MDM2-dependency association.\n\nFourth, MSI-high status is associated with markedly stronger WRN dependency. Accepted contrasts are about 0.77 to 0.82 units more negative, far above benchmark, and validated independently as well as internally replicated across clean genomic, high-quality, high-Cas9, mutation-burden, ploidy, interferon, proliferation, and library contexts.\n\nFifth, PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency. Accepted contrasts range roughly from 0.19 to 0.42 units more negative, above the STAT3 benchmark. This association is broad and stable across full, adenocarcinoma, high-quality, high-Cas9, TP53, PIK3CA, IFN, EMT, stemness, ploidy, serum, growth-rate, library, and clean-background analyses; several representative strata were independently validated. Interaction probes did not reliably establish clinically meaningful modifiers, so the stable conclusion is the main PTEN-loss-to-STAT3 association.\n\nSixth, CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency. Accepted contrasts are roughly 0.10 to 0.15 units more negative, exceeding the MDM2 benchmark and appearing consistently across TP53-intact, TP53-loss, MTAP-stratified, ploidy, growth-rate, mutation-burden, screen-quality, library, and clean-background analyses. This is the largest accepted MDM2 association and should be considered internally supported but not necessarily externally validated.\n\nA smaller accepted context-specific association is NF1 loss in KRAS-wild-type, higher-screen-quality lines, where KRAS dependency is about 0.061 units weaker than in NF1-intact KRAS-wild-type lines. This exceeds the KRAS practical benchmark at the point estimate but is restricted by eligibility and should be interpreted cautiously as a dataset-specific context effect.\n\nNegative or unsupported canonical expectations. BRAF V600E was not associated with stronger BRAF dependency in the accepted evidence. KRAS mutation did not show a robust accepted stronger KRAS dependency association overall or in major accepted refinements; the available KRAS-mutation results are small, inconsistent, or selected. ERBB2 amplification was not accepted for ERBB2 dependency, and EGFR amplification remains unresolved with wide or borderline validation intervals. MYC amplification was not associated with DHX9, RPL11, or POLR2A dependency, and KIF18A was not accepted. PIK3CA mutation was not accepted as a meaningful predictor of EGFR, ERBB2, or STAT3 dependency in the tested contexts. TP53 loss was not robustly associated with stronger MDM2 dependency. MYC amplification in high MYC-expression contexts also did not support DHX9 or RPL11 dependencies. The constructed research markers D, E, and F did not provide clinically meaningful STAT3 associations. Broad receptor-crosstalk, MSI-high DHX9, RB1-DHX9, BRCA2-DHX9, and many interaction hypotheses were null, below benchmark, or too imprecise to support.\n\nUnresolved uncertainty. The most informative unresolved candidates are EGFR amplification for dependency_EGFR, KRAS mutation for dependency_KRAS, broader NF1-loss effects in KRAS-wild-type KRAS dependency, RB1 loss with weaker DHX9 dependency, MTAP co-loss as a modifier within CDKN2A-loss lines, and possible interaction modifiers of PTEN/STAT3 or TP53/USP7 such as IFN, EMT, serum, AXL, growth rate, KRAS status, or expression markers. record.narrative: No assessments are currently due, and independent validation budget is exhausted, so the next internal experiments should focus on specificity, unresolved candidates, and biologically meaningful effect modification rather than further broad subgroup slicing. I registered seven new or refined comparisons. Two address previously unresolved but mechanistically plausible predictor-outcome pairs: RB1 loss with dependency_DHX9 in a relatively clean, high-quality background, expecting RB1 loss to be associated with weaker DHX9 dependency (less negative score); and NF1 loss with dependency_KRAS in KRAS-wild-type, higher-quality, co-alteration-restricted lines, expecting weaker KRAS dependency as a possible RAS-pathway bypass. A third tests whether KRAS-mutant lines show stronger KRAS dependency in a restricted canonical-background and higher-quality setting; prior KRAS-mutation estimates were inconsistent, so this is a falsifiable specificity test rather than a validation. A fourth tests the accepted PTEN-loss-to-stronger-STAT3 association in canonical oncogene-wild-type, higher-quality, higher-Cas9 lines to assess whether it remains apparent when common driver alterations are excluded. Two interaction probes test whether the robust CDKN2A-loss/MDM2 and SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 associations are stronger in MTAP-loss (within TP53-intact higher-quality lines) and high-aneuploidy contexts, respectively. The final comparison revisits EGFR amplification dependency_EGFR in a cleaner, ERBB2-negative, KRAS-wild-type, higher-quality background because EGFR remains one of the most informative unresolved candidates. For direction -1 claims, a positive signed result indicates stronger dependency (more negative score) in the exposed group or a stronger registered main effect in the named interaction subgroup; for direction +1 claims, a positive signed result indicates weaker dependency or a stronger weaker-dependency effect in the named subgroup. I used approximately 10% of the absolute mean dependency score as a practical benchmark. These proposals are intended to produce dataset-specific associations only, with interpretation constrained by multiplicity, selection from eligibility filters, and the absence of remaining independent validation capacity.

record.narrative:
All estimates are already signed to the registered direction. For direction -1 claims, a positive signed mean difference or interaction estimate supports stronger dependency in the exposed group or a stronger registered main effect in the interaction subgroup; for direction +1 claims, a positive signed estimate supports weaker dependency or a stronger weaker-dependency effect in the named subgroup. To apply the 10% clinical-significance instruction to negative dependency scores, I used approximately 10% of the absolute population mean dependency score for the relevant outcome as a practical magnitude benchmark. This is a heuristic because group means are not displayed, but it gives roughly: SMARCA2 about 0.042, USP7 about 0.018, STAT3 about 0.028, WRN about 0.030, MDM2 about 0.027, EGFR/ERBB2/KRAS/DHX9 about 0.025, and smaller for outcomes centered closer to zero.

H20 is accepted and closed. In Avana-library screens, SMARCA4 loss versus SMARCA4 intact shows a positive signed difference of +0.781 (95% Welch interval 0.760 to 0.802) for dependency_SMARCA2. This is far above the SMARCA2 benchmark and indicates markedly stronger SMARCA2 dependency in SMARCA4-loss lines. It reinforces the already robust dataset-specific SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 association within a common library context. Acceptance remains internal to this dataset and is not causal or external evidence.

H279 is accepted and closed with caution. In KRAS-wild-type, BRAF-wild-type, higher-screen-quality lines excluding TP53 loss, KEAP1 loss, MSI-high, SMARCA4 loss, and PTEN loss, NF1 loss versus NF1 intact shows a positive signed difference of +0.1118 (0.0357 to 0.1880) for dependency_KRAS with direction +1. This indicates weaker KRAS dependency among NF1-loss lines, far above the KRAS benchmark, and the interval excludes zero and the benchmark. The exposed cell is only 27, and the analysis is highly selected, so the claim is accepted only as a restricted dataset-specific association, not as a general NF1-loss effect or mechanism.

H281 is accepted and closed. In higher-screen-quality, higher-Cas9 lines without KRAS, BRAF, EGFR, or ERBB2 alterations, PTEN loss versus PTEN intact shows a positive signed difference of +0.2358 (0.0868 to 0.3847) for dependency_STAT3 with direction -1. This indicates substantially stronger STAT3 dependency among PTEN-loss lines in an oncogene-wild-type setting. The point estimate and lower bound are well above the STAT3 benchmark, despite exposed n=31. This supports robustness of the PTEN-loss/STAT3 association beyond common driver-altered backgrounds, but remains a dataset-specific association.

H50 is accepted and closed. In the adenocarcinoma/non-Avana subgroup, TP53 loss versus intact TP53 gives +0.3342 (0.0521 to 0.6164) for dependency_USP7 with direction +1. The interval is wide because exposed n=32 and comparator n=133, but the lower bound is above the USP7 benchmark and supports weaker USP7 dependency with TP53 loss. This is consistent with the broader internally supported TP53-loss/USP7 pattern. It is accepted only as an internal association in a small selected context.

H38 is rejected and closed. ARID1A loss overall versus ARID1A intact shows a negative signed estimate of -0.0168 (-0.0566 to 0.0229) for dependency_SMARCA2. The interval includes zero and the positive upper bound is below the SMARCA2 benchmark, so there is no evidence for a clinically meaningful stronger SMARCA2 dependency with ARID1A loss. The negative point estimate is not strong enough to establish the opposite effect; the registered direction is not supported.

H39 is rejected and closed. Overall NF1 loss versus intact NF1 gives a negative signed estimate of -0.0202 (-0.0491 to 0.0086) for dependency_KRAS with direction -1. This does not support stronger KRAS dependency with NF1 loss; the point estimate instead reflects the opposite direction, but the interval crosses zero and is not sufficiently precise to establish a clinically meaningful opposite effect. It is closed because it is inconsistent with the restricted KRAS-wild-type accepted context.

H36 is unresolved and closed because the non-Avana MSI-high versus MSS comparison has only 10 exposed observations, below the minimum-cell-size requirement, so it cannot be interpreted.

H278 is unresolved and closed. RB1 loss in a clean high-quality background gives +0.0396 (-0.0188 to 0.0980) for dependency_DHX9. The point estimate is near or above the DHX9 benchmark and suggests weaker DHX9 dependency, but the interval includes zero and is too imprecise given exposed n=45 and selection. No clinically meaningful dataset-specific association is accepted.

H280 is unresolved and closed. KRAS mutation in a restricted high-quality canonical-background set gives +0.0289 (-0.0110 to 0.0687) for dependency_KRAS. The point estimate is slightly above the KRAS benchmark but the interval includes zero and the result remains too uncertain to accept a stronger KRAS-dependency association, consistent with the inconsistent KRAS-mutation evidence overall.

H282 is unresolved and closed. The MTAP-loss interaction probe for CDKN2A-loss effects on MDM2 dependency within TP53-intact, higher-quality lines gives +0.0559 (-0.0899 to 0.2018). The point estimate exceeds the MDM2 benchmark, but the interval is very wide and crosses zero. This cannot establish clinically meaningful modification of the CDKN2A-loss/MDM2 association by MTAP co-loss.

H283 is rejected and closed. The high-aneuploidy interaction probe for SMARCA4-loss effects on SMARCA2 dependency gives -0.0257 (-0.0862 to 0.0348). The negative signed estimate is opposite the registered stronger-effect direction, and the positive upper bound is below the SMARCA2 benchmark. The evidence does not support clinically meaningful strengthening of the SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 association in high-aneuploidy lines.

H284 is unresolved and closed. In a cleaner high-quality background excluding KRAS mutation, ERBB2 amplification, TP53 loss, KEAP1 loss, and MSI-high, EGFR amplification gives +0.0130 (-0.0491 to 0.0751) for dependency_EGFR. The point estimate is below the EGFR benchmark and the interval is wide. This remains unresolved but should not be further expanded because EGFR amplification has produced borderline or null evidence across multiple selected contexts and multiplicity is high.

Audit: direct outcome leakage is unlikely, but these are observational cell-line associations. The highly filtered comparisons are vulnerable to selection and collider-like artifacts, especially H279, H281, and H50 with small exposed cells. Multiplicity is substantial, and independent validation budget is exhausted. Therefore, accepted claims are dataset-specific associations in defined eligibility or subgroup settings only; they are not causal, therapeutic, or generalizable claims. No validation was requested because no new validation capacity remains.

Iteration 23/25, stage synthesize, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

record.narrative:
No assessments are due and no independent-validation budget remains, so this final exploration phase registers targeted internal specificity, pathway-alternative, modifier, and robustness tests rather than attempting further validation. All estimates will be interpreted as signed to the registered direction. For direction -1 claims, a positive signed mean difference indicates raw more-negative values in the exposed group, i.e. stronger dependency; for direction +1 claims, a positive signed estimate indicates raw higher/less-negative values, i.e. weaker dependency. For interactions, the raw contrast is the named-subgroup contrast minus the same-population complement contrast, and it is then signed to the registered interaction direction.

The EGFR amplification association remains borderline rather than accepted. I therefore registered an interaction by KRAS-mutation status. Because EGFR dependence may be strongest in an EGFR-amplified, KRAS-wild-type background and weaker when KRAS mutation provides parallel RAS-pathway activation, the named subgroup is KRAS-wild-type and direction is -1. A positive signed estimate would mean the EGFR-amplified versus EGFR-negative contrast is more negative in KRAS-wild-type lines than in KRAS-mutant lines. This is a specificity test for the unresolved EGFR amplification signal, not a new overall main-effect claim.

Two RAS-pathway probes address underexamined dependency_RIT1 associations. First, I test whether KRAS mutation is associated with stronger RIT1 dependency in a restricted high-screen-quality, high-Cas9, relatively co-mutation-clean background. RIT1 is a RAS-family GTPase, so a KRAS-mutant effect could reflect pathway co-dependence, but earlier KRAS-mutation estimates were inconsistent; this test is falsifiable and expected to be null unless the association is concentrated in cleaner high-quality lines. Second, I test NF1 loss among KRAS-wild-type high-quality lines for RIT1 dependency. If NF1 loss activates alternative RAS signaling, it may bypass RIT1 dependency and produce a less-negative score, so direction is +1. This is an internal mechanistic alternative to the accepted restricted NF1-loss/KRAS-dependency association, not evidence of generalizability.

I registered one high-quality/cleaned follow-up for MYC amplification and KIF18A dependency. MYC amplification was broadly null overall for mitotic and transcriptional outcomes, but if there is a clinically meaningful proliferative/mitotic dependency effect, it might be more visible under high screen quality and adequate Cas9 activity. The expected direction is -1 for stronger KIF18A dependency, but the prior broad null and modest effect-size benchmark make this an unresolved specificity probe.

For accepted PTEN loss and STAT3 dependency, I registered an interaction by PIK3CA mutation status to test pathway independence. PTEN loss and PIK3CA mutation both affect PI3K/AKT signaling, and prior stratified estimates suggested the PTEN effect may persist in both PIK3CA-mutant and PIK3CA-wild-type contexts. The registered direction is -1, but anticipated modification is zero: a large positive estimate would indicate stronger PTEN loss effect in PIK3CA-mutant lines, a large negative estimate stronger effect in PIK3CA-wild-type lines, and an estimate near zero would support robustness across PI3K-pathway genetic context.

I registered two specificity controls for accepted associations. KEAP1 loss with WRN dependency and TP53 loss with NFE2L2 dependency in high-quality screens are negative-control probes: if the accepted KEAP1/NFE2L2 and TP53/USP7 associations are reasonably specific, these effects should be near zero or below practical magnitude. Direction and anticipated direction are registered mainly to provide signed outputs, with anticipated zero indicating no expected clinically meaningful effect.

Finally, I registered WRN dependency in MSI-high versus MSS under lower screen quality as a robustness probe for the accepted MSI-high/WRN association. The main accepted association is robust in high-quality and several co-mutation-restricted contexts, but lower-quality screens could attenuate it. If the association persists even with lower screen quality, it supports internal robustness; if attenuated, the accepted high-quality finding may depend partly on screen quality. All proposed claims remain dataset-specific associations and are vulnerable to multiplicity and selection artifacts.

The practical magnitude benchmark remains approximately 10% of the absolute mean dependency score: roughly 0.025 for EGFR, KRAS, DHX9, ERBB2, POLR2A, RIT1, RPL11, TMED10, and KIF18A; 0.028 for STAT3; 0.030 for WRN; 0.018 for USP7; 0.042 for SMARCA2; and 0.009 for NFE2L2. Because validation budget is exhausted, none of these proposals is intended to convert unresolved claims into externally validated claims.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.

status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.

changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due

For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

All estimates will be interpreted as signed to the registered direction. For direction -1 claims, a positive signed mean difference indicates raw more-negative values in the exposed group, i.e. stronger dependency; for direction +1 claims, a positive signed estimate indicates raw higher/less-negative values, i.e. weaker dependency. For interactions, the raw contrast is the named-subgroup contrast minus the same-population complement contrast, and it is then signed to the registered interaction direction.\n\nThe EGFR amplification association remains borderline rather than accepted. I therefore registered an interaction by KRAS-mutation status. Because EGFR dependence may be strongest in an EGFR-amplified, KRAS-wild-type background and weaker when KRAS mutation provides parallel RAS-pathway activation, the named subgroup is KRAS-wild-type and direction is -1. A positive signed estimate would mean the EGFR-amplified versus EGFR-negative contrast is more negative in KRAS-wild-type lines than in KRAS-mutant lines. This is a specificity test for the unresolved EGFR amplification signal, not a new overall main-effect claim.\n\nTwo RAS-pathway probes address underexamined dependency_RIT1 associations. First, I test whether KRAS mutation is associated with stronger RIT1 dependency in a restricted high-screen-quality, high-Cas9, relatively co-mutation-clean background. RIT1 is a RAS-family GTPase, so a KRAS-mutant effect could reflect pathway co-dependence, but earlier KRAS-mutation estimates were inconsistent; this test is falsifiable and expected to be null unless the association is concentrated in cleaner high-quality lines. Second, I test NF1 loss among KRAS-wild-type high-quality lines for RIT1 dependency. If NF1 loss activates alternative RAS signaling, it may bypass RIT1 dependency and produce a less-negative score, so direction is +1. This is an internal mechanistic alternative to the accepted restricted NF1-loss/KRAS-dependency association, not evidence of generalizability.\n\nI registered one high-quality/cleaned follow-up for MYC amplification and KIF18A dependency. MYC amplification was broadly null overall for mitotic and transcriptional outcomes, but if there is a clinically meaningful proliferative/mitotic dependency effect, it might be more visible under high screen quality and adequate Cas9 activity. The expected direction is -1 for stronger KIF18A dependency, but the prior broad null and modest effect-size benchmark make this an unresolved specificity probe.\n\nFor accepted PTEN loss and STAT3 dependency, I registered an interaction by PIK3CA mutation status to test pathway independence. PTEN loss and PIK3CA mutation both affect PI3K/AKT signaling, and prior stratified estimates suggested the PTEN effect may persist in both PIK3CA-mutant and PIK3CA-wild-type contexts. The registered direction is -1, but anticipated modification is zero: a large positive estimate would indicate stronger PTEN loss effect in PIK3CA-mutant lines, a large negative estimate stronger effect in PIK3CA-wild-type lines, and an estimate near zero would support robustness across PI3K-pathway genetic context.\n\nI registered two specificity controls for accepted associations. KEAP1 loss with WRN dependency and TP53 loss with NFE2L2 dependency in high-quality screens are negative-control probes: if the accepted KEAP1/NFE2L2 and TP53/USP7 associations are reasonably specific, these effects should be near zero or below practical magnitude. Direction and anticipated direction are registered mainly to provide signed outputs, with anticipated zero indicating no expected clinically meaningful effect.\n\nFinally, I registered WRN dependency in MSI-high versus MSS under lower screen quality as a robustness probe for the accepted MSI-high/WRN association. The main accepted association is robust in high-quality and several co-mutation-restricted contexts, but lower-quality screens could attenuate it. If the association persists even with lower screen quality, it supports internal robustness; if attenuated, the accepted high-quality finding may depend partly on screen quality. record.narrative:
All estimates are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction. For direction -1 mean differences, a positive signed estimate supports stronger dependency in the exposed group; for direction +1 mean differences, a positive signed estimate supports weaker dependency in the exposed group. For interactions, a positive signed estimate supports a stronger effect in the named subgroup relative to its complement, in the registered direction. I used approximately 10% of the absolute population mean dependency score as a practical benchmark, yielding roughly 0.025 for EGFR/RIT1/KIF18A, 0.028 for STAT3, 0.030 for WRN, 0.009 for NFE2L2, 0.042 for SMARCA2, and 0.018 for USP7. These are dataset-specific associations only; no causal, therapeutic, or external generalization is inferred. No validation was requested because the new validation budget is zero.

H285 is rejected and closed. The EGFR-amplification-by-KRAS-wild-type interaction for dependency_EGFR gives a negative signed estimate of -0.0372 (95% CI -0.0949 to 0.0205), opposite the registered stronger-effect direction. The upper bound is below the EGFR practical benchmark of about 0.025, so there is no evidence for a clinically meaningful interaction in the registered direction. Because the interval still includes zero and the reversed interaction was not pre-specified as a new claim, I close this branch rather than propose a reversal.

H286 is unresolved and closed. KRAS mutation versus KRAS wild type in high-screen-quality, high-Cas9, relatively clean co-mutation backgrounds gives a positive signed estimate of +0.0391 for dependency_RIT1, suggesting stronger RIT1 dependency among KRAS-mutant lines, but the interval (-0.0074 to 0.0855) crosses zero and exposed/comparator cells are modest. It is too uncertain to accept despite exceeding the RIT1 benchmark in the point estimate. This is consistent with the broader inconsistency of KRAS-mutation predictors and should not be expanded further.

H287 is unresolved and closed. NF1 loss among KRAS-wild-type, high-screen-quality lines gives +0.0183 for dependency_RIT1, nominally in the predicted weaker-dependency direction, but the interval (-0.0283 to 0.0650) includes zero and the point estimate is below the RIT1 practical benchmark. This does not support a clinically meaningful RIT1 modification by NF1 loss in this context.

H288 is unresolved and closed. MYC amplification in high-screen-quality, high-Cas9 backgrounds gives +0.0302 for dependency_KIF18A, above the KIF18A benchmark, but the interval (-0.0135 to 0.0740) includes zero and is imprecise. Given the prior broad null for MYC amplification across mitotic and transcriptional outcomes, this is a underpowered specificity probe, not a new accepted association.

H289 is unresolved and closed. The PIK3CA-mutation interaction probe for PTEN-loss effects on dependency_STAT3 gives an estimate very close to zero, +0.0013 (95% CI -0.1499 to 0.1524). The point estimate suggests no meaningful modification of the accepted PTEN-loss/STAT3 association, but the interval is too wide to rule out a large interaction in either direction. This neither supports nor refutes a stable PI3K-pathway modifier; it leaves modifier uncertainty unresolved.

H290 is rejected and closed as a specificity control. KEAP1 loss versus KEAP1 intact in high-screen-quality screens gives -0.0206 for dependency_WRN, opposite the registered weaker-dependency direction, with the positive upper bound (0.0201) below the WRN benchmark. There is no clinically meaningful evidence that KEAP1 loss produces a WRN-dependency signal analogous to the accepted KEAP1/NFE2L2 association.

H291 is unresolved and closed. TP53 loss versus intact TP53 in high-screen-quality screens gives +0.0159 for dependency_NFE2L2, nominally above the small NFE2L2 benchmark but with an interval (-0.0367 to 0.0685) that includes zero. This negative-control probe is too imprecise to accept a clinically meaningful TP53-loss/NFE2L2-dependency association, although it does not strongly rule one out either.

H292 is accepted and closed. MSI-high versus non-MSI-high lines under lower screen quality show a very large positive signed difference for dependency_WRN, +0.7813 (95% CI 0.7303 to 0.8323), far above the WRN benchmark and excluding zero. This provides strong internal robustness evidence that the MSI-high/WRN association is not confined only to higher-screen-quality subsets. It remains a dataset-specific association, not evidence of external biological mechanism or clinical utility.

H104-H106 assess constructed research markers D, E, and F as negative-control probes. H104 is rejected and closed: research marker D gives +0.0024 for dependency_SMARCA2 (95% CI -0.0298 to 0.0345), and the upper bound is below the SMARCA2 benchmark. H105 is rejected and closed: research marker E gives -0.0126 for dependency_WRN (95% CI -0.0356 to 0.0105), and the positive upper bound is below the WRN benchmark. H106 is unresolved and closed: research marker F gives +0.0194 for dependency_USP7 (95% CI -0.0153 to 0.0541), crossing zero despite a point estimate slightly above the USP7 benchmark. Overall, these constructed markers do not provide supported predictor signals, supporting specificity for the accepted genetic associations, with the minor caveat that marker F remains imprecise.

Overall, this batch leaves one clear new accepted robustness result (MSI-high/WRN in lower screen quality) and otherwise closes specificity, modifier, negative-control, and marker probes as unsupported or unresolved. Multiplicity and selection are major caveats, especially for highly filtered KRAS and PTEN context analyses. No new validation request is possible or warranted.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

record.narrative:
No response deadlines were listed, no new validation estimates were delivered during this synthesis step, and the independent-validation budget is exhausted. I therefore made no validation requests and made no status changes. The final synthesis is based on the full discovery/validation ledger and should be read as internal associations within the supplied lung-lineage CRISPR dataset, not as causal effects, therapeutic vulnerabilities, or generalizable biological claims. Where independent validation exists, it supports internal reproducibility of the stated direction and magnitude, not external validity.

All returned estimates are already signed to the hypothesis direction. For direction -1 mean differences, a positive signed estimate indicates a raw more-negative dependency score in the exposed group, i.e. stronger dependency. For direction +1 mean differences, a positive signed estimate indicates a raw less-negative dependency score in the exposed group, i.e. weaker dependency. I continued to use roughly 10% of the absolute mean dependency score as a practical benchmark, approximately 0.042 for SMARCA2, 0.030 for WRN, 0.028 for STAT3, 0.025 for KRAS/EGFR/ERBB2/DHX9/POLR2A/RPL11/RIT1/KIF18A, 0.018 for USP7, and 0.009 for NFE2L2. Acceptance required a meaningful point estimate, a 95% interval excluding zero, cell-size validity, and enough consistency to survive multiplicity and selection concerns.

SUPPORTED DATASET-SPECIFIC ASSOCIATIONS:
1. SMARCA4 loss is strongly associated with SMARCA2 dependency. The contrast is approximately 0.75 to 0.82 dependency-score units more negative, far above the SMARCA2 benchmark. This is the most robust accepted association and is supported across library, screen-quality, Cas9-activity, lineage, co-alteration, growth-rate, expression, ploidy, and aneuploidy strata; independent validation in a higher screen-quality stratum gives about 0.81, with the interval still excluding zero (R31/R40). Interpretation: internal co-dependency signal, not validated clinical synthetic lethality outside this dataset.
2. KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency. The accepted direction is the reverse of the original stronger-dependency hypothesis: H22 accepts a positive signed contrast of about 0.78 to 0.81, corresponding to raw less-negative scores, i.e. reduced dependency (R6/R26). This result is independently validated and is robust across lineage, screen-quality, Cas9-activity, library, co-alteration, growth-rate, EMT, and clean-background contexts. The original H6 direction is rejected because it asks for a stronger-dependency effect that the data do not support.
3. TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency. The accepted signed contrast is roughly 0.27 to 0.49, corresponding to raw less-negative USP7 scores (R8/R39). It is robust across library, screen quality, Cas9 activity, lineage, ploidy, growth rate, co-mutation, EMT, AXL expression, MYC expression, interferon, and other strata, with several independent validations. A small negative control using TP53 loss and NFE2L2 was unresolved but does not support an analogous cross-pathway signal.
4. MSI-high status is associated with markedly stronger WRN dependency. The accepted signed contrast is approximately 0.77 to 0.83, far above the WRN benchmark (R9/R53). The association replicates in adenocarcinoma, higher screen quality, high Cas9 activity, mutation-burden, ploidy, interferon, proliferation, lower screen quality, and co-mutation-restricted analyses, including H292 in lower-quality screens (R296). It is independently validated. This is a very strong internal association, but the evidence does not show external biological mechanism or clinical utility.
5. PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency. Accepted contrasts are roughly 0.19 to 0.51 signed units, corresponding to raw more-negative STAT3 scores. Several representative contexts are independently validated, including overall high-quality screens, low Cas9 activity, TP53-loss, PIK3CA-mutant, PIK3CA-wild-type, high IFN-gamma, EMT, stemness, proliferation, and clean high-quality contexts (for example R80/R66, R109/R107, R113/R106, R123/R120, R132/R133). Modifier probes did not establish a stable interaction, so PTEN loss should be interpreted as the robust predictor in this dataset rather than a context that necessarily modifies or is modified by other accepted markers.
6. CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency. Accepted signed contrasts are approximately 0.10 to 0.16, corresponding to raw more-negative MDM2 scores (R168/R177/R183/R178/R185/R209/R219/R234/R270). This is consistent across TP53-intact and TP53-loss contexts, ploidy strata, mutation burden, growth rate, Cas9 activity, screen quality, MTAP stratification, and relatively clean co-mutation backgrounds. It was not independently validated, but it is internally consistent and far below the null benchmark. It should be described as an association, not a causal mechanism.
7. NF1 loss is associated with weaker KRAS dependency in restricted KRAS-wild-type, higher-screen-quality settings. The accepted signed contrasts are about 0.06 to 0.11 for KRAS-wild-type high-quality and highly restricted backgrounds (R246/R278), corresponding to raw less-negative KRAS scores. This finding should be narrowly interpreted because of eligibility selection, small exposed cells, and the broader inconsistency of KRAS-pathway predictors. It is not validated and should not be generalized beyond the selected KRAS-wild-type context.

NEGATIVE OR UNSUPPORTED FINDINGS:
The canonical alteration-own-dependency hypotheses were not supported as robust associations. Broad KRAS mutation versus wild type for KRAS dependency remained unresolved/inconsistent (R1/R262/R264/R279), and BRAF V600E was not supported for BRAF dependency (R2/R104). EGFR amplification remains unresolved rather than accepted: the main discovery estimate is borderline and validation is too wide to confirm (R3/R13), while cleaner or background-stratified probes are null or imprecise. ERBB2 amplification for ERBB2 dependency is near zero and not meaningful (R4). TP53 loss was not robustly associated with stronger MDM2 dependency (R7/R26/R50/R49/R78), in contrast to the supported CDKN2A-loss/MDM2 association. MYC amplification showed no meaningful association with DHX9, RPL11, POLR2A, or KIF18A, including in high MYC expression or higher-screen-quality contexts (R10-R12/R14/R119/R124/R132/R292). PIK3CA mutation was not accepted as a meaningful predictor of STAT3, EGFR, or ERBB2 dependency (R63/R130/R242/R243). Constructed research markers D, E, and F did not provide supported STAT3 or cross-outcome predictors; marker D and E were rejected against their probes, and marker F remained imprecise and unsupported (R88-R90/R297-R299). Most interaction probes for lineage, library, Cas9 activity, growth rate, aneuploidy, IFN-gamma, EMT, AXL, serum, MTAP, PIK3CA, and co-alteration contexts did not establish clinically meaningful modification. In particular, EGFR-amplification interaction by KRAS status rejected the registered interaction (R289), SMARCA4/SMARCA2 interactions were null, TP53/USP7 interactions were unsupported, and the PTEN/STAT3 PIK3CA interaction was near zero but too imprecise to establish or exclude modification.

UNRESOLVED UNCERTAINTY:
EGFR amplification remains borderline: discovery and validation intervals are too wide or close to zero to accept, and specificity probes did not identify a clean context that rescues the signal. KRAS mutation effects remain inconsistent; a high-Cas9 KRAS-mutant/KRAS-dependency estimate is directionally meaningful but not accepted because of prior broad nulls and selection concerns. NF1 loss effects outside selected KRAS-wild-type high-quality contexts remain unresolved. RB1-loss/DHX9 dependency, broader TP53-loss/NFE2L2 cross-pathway controls, and some high-IFN or expression-stratified signals remain imprecise or too underpowered. MTAP modification of CDKN2A-loss/MDM2 dependency remains unresolved because interaction intervals are wide. Modifier interactions for PTEN/STAT3 and TP53/USP7 remain unresolved or unsupported. Finally, the accepted context-specific associations remain vulnerable to multiplicity, collider-like selection, and residual confounding by screen or genomic features, even after many stratified checks.

FINAL SCIENTIFIC STANCE:
The dataset provides strong internal evidence for associations involving SMARCA4 loss/SMARCA2, KEAP1 loss/NFE2L2 reverse direction, TP53 loss/USP7 reverse direction, MSI-high/WRN, PTEN loss/STAT3, CDKN2A loss/MDM2, and a narrow NF1-loss/KRAS-wild-type association. These are the main supported findings. Canonical mutation- or amplification-own-dependency relationships are not robustly supported in this dataset. No claim should be stated as causal, therapeutic, or generalizable without independent external replication.

MOST INFORMATIVE NEXT ANALYSIS:
The highest-value follow-up is external or truly independent replication of the six main accepted associations and the narrow NF1-loss association, with pre-specified models adjusting for library, screen quality, Cas9 activity, lineage, ploidy, mutation burden, proliferation, and co-occurring SMARCA4/KEAP1/TP53/MSI/PTEN/CDKN2A/MTAP/NF1/KRAS/EGFR/ERBB2 alterations. If only internal work is possible, further analysis should be pre-specified on unresolved candidates only, with adequate cell sizes, multiplicity control, and no additional broad subgroup slicing.

record.narrative:
No assessments are due and no new validation budget remains, so this final exploration registers 12 internal probes only. All estimates are already signed to the registered direction. For direction -1, a positive signed mean difference means the exposed group is raw more negative, i.e. stronger dependency; for direction +1, a positive signed mean difference means the exposed group is raw less negative, i.e. weaker dependency. Interactions are signed to the registered direction, and practical importance is judged against roughly 10% of the absolute mean dependency score (about 0.025-0.030 for MDM2/STAT3/WRN/KRAS, 0.018 for USP7, 0.009 for NFE2L2, and 0.042 for SMARCA2).

First, I registered low-screen-quality robustness checks for accepted core associations: PTEN loss/STAT3, CDKN2A loss/MDM2, KEAP1 loss/NFE2L2 reverse direction, TP53 loss/USP7 reverse direction, and NF1 loss/KRAS in KRAS-wild-type backgrounds. The aim is internal quality robustness, not external generalization. Similarly, MSI-high/WRN is checked under lower Cas9 activity to test whether the very large accepted association persists when editing efficiency is less favorable.

Second, I added a NRF2-pathway probe: KEAP1 loss versus STAT3 dependency under high screen quality and adequate Cas9 activity. KEAP1 loss is biologically plausible as a modifier of STAT3 through NRF2-driven oxidative-stress responses, but prior data do not establish direction. The registered direction +1 expresses the hypothesis that KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker STAT3 dependency, while anticipated_direction=0 reflects uncertainty and the risk that this is a null control.

Third, I registered two PI3K-AKT/MDM2 pathway hypotheses: PIK3CA mutation and PTEN loss versus MDM2 dependency in high-quality, TP53-intact lines. PI3K/AKT activation can upregulate or functionally activate MDM2, and p53 wild-type status should make MDM2 dependency more meaningful. The registered direction -1 is stronger MDM2 dependency in the PI3K-activated exposure. These tests are specific because PIK3CA was not robust for STAT3/EGFR/ERBB2 outcomes and PTEN has a robust STAT3 association; if PTEN loss also shifts MDM2, that would broaden the dataset-specific PTEN signal.

Fourth, I probed CDKN2A/MDM2 context further: MTAP loss among CDKN2A-intact lines, and a high-quality interaction by PTEN loss. MTAP deletion often co-occurs with CDKN2A loss, and PTEN loss is a separate strong dependency predictor; both are registered as modifier or specificity probes with anticipated zero modification unless there is a meaningful interaction.

Finally, I added an adherent-culture robustness check for SMARCA4 loss/SMARCA2 because growth/culture state can bias CRISPR screens and dependency measurements. This is not a new biological mechanism claim. All proposals remain dataset-specific associations, vulnerable to multiplicity, residual confounding, and selection effects, and none will be interpreted as causal or clinically generalizable without independent external replication.

Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

Focus: low-screen-quality/low-Cas9 robustness for accepted SMARCA2, NFE2L2 reverse, USP7 reverse, WRN, STAT3, MDM2/CDKN2A, KRAS/NF1; new PI3K-AKT/MDM2 tests (PIK3CA and PTEN in TP53-intact high-quality); KEAP1-STAT3 plausible but uncertain; MTAP among CDKN2A-intact; PTEN interaction with CDKN2A-MDM2; adherent-culture robustness for SMARCA4-SMARCA2.","latest_stage_narratives":{"explore":"No assessments are due and no new validation budget remains, so this final exploration registers 12 internal probes only. All estimates are already signed to the registered direction. For direction -1, a positive signed mean difference means the exposed group is raw more negative, i.e. stronger dependency; for direction +1, a positive signed mean difference means the exposed group is raw less negative, i.e. weaker dependency. Interactions are signed to the registered direction, and practical importance is judged against roughly 10% of the absolute mean dependency score (about 0.025-0.030 for MDM2/STAT3/WRN/KRAS, 0.018 for USP7, 0.009 for NFE2L2, and 0.042 for SMARCA2).\n\nFirst, I registered low-screen-quality robustness checks for accepted core associations: PTEN loss/STAT3, CDKN2A loss/MDM2, KEAP1 loss/NFE2L2 reverse direction, TP53 loss/USP7 reverse direction, and NF1 loss/KRAS in KRAS-wild-type backgrounds. The aim is internal quality robustness, not external generalization. Similarly, MSI-high/WRN is checked under lower Cas9 activity to test whether the very large accepted association persists when editing efficiency is less favorable.\n\nSecond, I added a NRF2-pathway probe: KEAP1 loss versus STAT3 dependency under high screen quality and adequate Cas9 activity. KEAP1 loss is biologically plausible as a modifier of STAT3 through NRF2-driven oxidative-stress responses, but prior data do not establish direction. The registered direction +1 expresses the hypothesis that KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker STAT3 dependency, while anticipated_direction=0 reflects uncertainty and the risk that this is a null control.\n\nThird, I registered two PI3K-AKT/MDM2 pathway hypotheses: PIK3CA mutation and PTEN loss versus MDM2 dependency in high-quality, TP53-intact lines. PI3K/AKT activation can upregulate or functionally activate MDM2, and p53 wild-type status should make MDM2 dependency more meaningful. The registered direction -1 is stronger MDM2 dependency in the PI3K-activated exposure. These tests are specific because PIK3CA was not robust for STAT3/EGFR/ERBB2 outcomes and PTEN has a robust STAT3 association; if PTEN loss also shifts MDM2, that would broaden the dataset-specific PTEN signal.\n\nFourth, I probed CDKN2A/MDM2 context further: MTAP loss among CDKN2A-intact lines, and a high-quality interaction by PTEN loss. MTAP deletion often co-occurs with CDKN2A loss, and PTEN loss is a separate strong dependency predictor; both are registered as modifier or specificity probes with anticipated zero modification unless there is a meaningful interaction.\n\nFinally, I added an adherent-culture robustness check for SMARCA4 loss/SMARCA2 because growth/culture state can bias CRISPR screens and dependency measurements. This is not a new biological mechanism claim. All proposals remain dataset-specific associations, vulnerable to multiplicity, residual confounding, and selection effects, and none will be interpreted as causal or clinically generalizable without independent external replication.","analyze":"No assessments are due, so I register no status changes and request analyses on all currently active untested specificity probes plus the three remaining untested research-marker specificity controls. H286 and H287 probe underexamined RAS-pathway associations with dependency_RIT1 in high-quality settings. H288 tests whether a MYC-amplification/KIF18A association emerges only under high screen quality and adequate Cas9 activity after broader null results. H289 tests whether the accepted PTEN-loss/STAT3 association is modified by PIK3CA mutation status. H290 and H291 are cross-pathway negative controls for the accepted KEAP1/NFE2L2 and TP53/USP7 associations. H292 tests robustness of the MSI-high/WRN association in lower-screen-quality lines. H104-H106 complete marker specificity assessment by testing constructed research markers D, E, and F against SMARCA2, WRN, and USP7 outcomes. All estimates will be interpreted as signed to the registered direction. Positive direction -1 mean-difference evidence indicates stronger dependency; positive direction +1 evidence indicates weaker dependency. For interactions, positive evidence indicates a stronger registered effect in the named subgroup relative to its complement. I will apply the practical magnitude benchmark of about 10% of the absolute mean dependency score for each outcome and require exclusion of zero and sufficient cell sizes before acceptance. These are dataset-specific associations only; no causal, therapeutic, or external generalization is claimed, and validation budget is exhausted.","appraise":"All estimates are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction. For direction -1 mean differences, a positive signed estimate supports stronger dependency in the exposed group; for direction +1 mean differences, a positive signed estimate supports weaker dependency in the exposed group. For interactions, a positive signed estimate supports a stronger effect in the named subgroup relative to its complement, in the registered direction. I used approximately 10% of the absolute population mean dependency score as a practical benchmark, yielding roughly 0.025 for EGFR/RIT1/KIF18A, 0.028 for STAT3, 0.030 for WRN, 0.009 for NFE2L2, 0.042 for SMARCA2, and 0.018 for USP7. These are dataset-specific associations only; no causal, therapeutic, or external generalization is inferred. No validation was requested because the new validation budget is zero.\n\nH285 is rejected and closed. The EGFR-amplification-by-KRAS-wild-type interaction for dependency_EGFR gives a negative signed estimate of -0.0372 (95% CI -0.0949 to 0.0205), opposite the registered stronger-effect direction. The upper bound is below the EGFR practical benchmark of about 0.025, so there is no evidence for a clinically meaningful interaction in the registered direction. Because the interval still includes zero and the reversed interaction was not pre-specified as a new claim, I close this branch rather than propose a reversal.\n\nH286 is unresolved and closed. KRAS mutation versus KRAS wild type in high-screen-quality, high-Cas9, relatively clean co-mutation backgrounds gives a positive signed estimate of +0.0391 for dependency_RIT1, suggesting stronger RIT1 dependency among KRAS-mutant lines, but the interval (-0.0074 to 0.0855) crosses zero and exposed/comparator cells are modest. It is too uncertain to accept despite exceeding the RIT1 benchmark in the point estimate. This is consistent with the broader inconsistency of KRAS-mutation predictors and should not be expanded further.\n\nH287 is unresolved and closed. NF1 loss among KRAS-wild-type, high-screen-quality lines gives +0.0183 for dependency_RIT1, nominally in the predicted weaker-dependency direction, but the interval (-0.0283 to 0.0650) includes zero and the point estimate is below the RIT1 practical benchmark. This does not support a clinically meaningful RIT1 modification by NF1 loss in this context.\n\nH288 is unresolved and closed. MYC amplification in high-screen-quality, high-Cas9 backgrounds gives +0.0302 for dependency_KIF18A, above the KIF18A benchmark, but the interval (-0.0135 to 0.0740) includes zero and is imprecise. Given the prior broad null for MYC amplification across mitotic and transcriptional outcomes, this is a underpowered specificity probe, not a new accepted association.\n\nH289 is unresolved and closed. The PIK3CA-mutation interaction probe for PTEN-loss effects on dependency_STAT3 gives an estimate very close to zero, +0.0013 (95% CI -0.1499 to 0.1524). The point estimate suggests no meaningful modification of the accepted PTEN-loss/STAT3 association, but the interval is too wide to rule out a large interaction in either direction. This neither supports nor refutes a stable PI3K-pathway modifier; it leaves modifier uncertainty unresolved.\n\nH290 is rejected and closed as a specificity control. KEAP1 loss versus KEAP1 intact in high-screen-quality screens gives -0.0206 for dependency_WRN, opposite the registered weaker-dependency direction, with the positive upper bound (0.0201) below the WRN benchmark. There is no clinically meaningful evidence that KEAP1 loss produces a WRN-dependency signal analogous to the accepted KEAP1/NFE2L2 association.\n\nH291 is unresolved and closed. TP53 loss versus intact TP53 in high-screen-quality screens gives +0.0159 for dependency_NFE2L2, nominally above the small NFE2L2 benchmark but with an interval (-0.0367 to 0.0685) that includes zero. This negative-control probe is too imprecise to accept a clinically meaningful TP53-loss/NFE2L2-dependency association, although it does not strongly rule one out either.\n\nH292 is accepted and closed. MSI-high versus non-MSI-high lines under lower screen quality show a very large positive signed difference for dependency_WRN, +0.7813 (95% CI 0.7303 to 0.8323), far above the WRN benchmark and excluding zero. This provides strong internal robustness evidence that the MSI-high/WRN association is not confined only to higher-screen-quality subsets. It remains a dataset-specific association, not evidence of external biological mechanism or clinical utility.\n\nH104-H106 assess constructed research markers D, E, and F as negative-control probes. H104 is rejected and closed: research marker D gives +0.0024 for dependency_SMARCA2 (95% CI -0.0298 to 0.0345), and the upper bound is below the SMARCA2 benchmark. H105 is rejected and closed: research marker E gives -0.0126 for dependency_WRN (95% CI -0.0356 to 0.0105), and the positive upper bound is below the WRN benchmark. H106 is unresolved and closed: research marker F gives +0.0194 for dependency_USP7 (95% CI -0.0153 to 0.0541), crossing zero despite a point estimate slightly above the USP7 benchmark. Overall, these constructed markers do not provide supported predictor signals, supporting specificity for the accepted genetic associations, with the minor caveat that marker F remains imprecise.\n\nOverall, this batch leaves one clear new accepted robustness result (MSI-high/WRN in lower screen quality) and otherwise closes specificity, modifier, negative-control, and marker probes as unsupported or unresolved. Multiplicity and selection are major caveats, especially for highly filtered KRAS and PTEN context analyses. No new validation request is possible or warranted.","synthesize":"No response deadlines were listed, no new validation estimates were delivered during this synthesis step, and the independent-validation budget is exhausted. Where independent validation exists, it supports internal reproducibility of the stated direction and magnitude, not external validity.\\n\\nAll returned estimates are already signed to the hypothesis direction. For direction -1 mean differences, a positive signed estimate indicates a raw more-negative dependency score in the exposed group, i.e. stronger dependency. For direction +1 mean differences, a positive signed estimate indicates a raw less-negative dependency score in the exposed group, i.e. weaker dependency. I continued to use roughly 10% of the absolute mean dependency score as a practical benchmark, approximately 0.042 for SMARCA2, 0.030 for WRN, 0.028 for STAT3, 0.025 for KRAS/EGFR/ERBB2/DHX9/POLR2A/RPL11/RIT1/KIF18A, 0.018 for USP7, and 0.009 for NFE2L2. Acceptance required a meaningful point estimate, a 95% interval excluding zero, cell-size validity, and enough consistency to survive multiplicity and selection concerns.\\n\\nSUPPORTED DATASET-SPECIFIC ASSOCIATIONS:\\n1. SMARCA4 loss is strongly associated with SMARCA2 dependency. The contrast is approximately 0.75 to 0.82 dependency-score units more negative, far above the SMARCA2 benchmark. This is the most robust accepted association and is supported across library, screen-quality, Cas9-activity, lineage, co-alteration, growth-rate, expression, ploidy, and aneuploidy strata; independent validation in a higher screen-quality stratum gives about 0.81, with the interval still excluding zero (R31/R40). Interpretation: internal co-dependency signal, not validated clinical synthetic lethality outside this dataset.\\n2. KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency. The accepted direction is the reverse of the original stronger-dependency hypothesis: H22 accepts a positive signed contrast of about 0.78 to 0.81, corresponding to raw less-negative scores, i.e. reduced dependency (R6/R26). This result is independently validated and is robust across lineage, screen-quality, Cas9-activity, library, co-alteration, growth-rate, EMT, and clean-background contexts. The original H6 direction is rejected because it asks for a stronger-dependency effect that the data do not support.\\n3. TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency. The accepted signed contrast is roughly 0.27 to 0.49, corresponding to raw less-negative USP7 scores (R8/R39). It is robust across library, screen quality, Cas9 activity, lineage, ploidy, growth rate, co-mutation, EMT, AXL expression, MYC expression, interferon, and other strata, with several independent validations. A small negative control using TP53 loss and NFE2L2 was unresolved but does not support an analogous cross-pathway signal.\\n4. MSI-high status is associated with markedly stronger WRN dependency. The accepted signed contrast is approximately 0.77 to 0.83, far above the WRN benchmark (R9/R53). The association replicates in adenocarcinoma, higher screen quality, high Cas9 activity, mutation-burden, ploidy, interferon, proliferation, lower screen quality, and co-mutation-restricted analyses, including H292 in lower-quality screens (R296). It is independently validated. This is a very strong internal association, but the evidence does not show external biological mechanism or clinical utility.\\n5. PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency. Accepted contrasts are roughly 0.19 to 0.51 signed units, corresponding to raw more-negative STAT3 scores. Several representative contexts are independently validated, including overall high-quality screens, low Cas9 activity, TP53-loss, PIK3CA-mutant, PIK3CA-wild-type, high IFN-gamma, EMT, stemness, proliferation, and clean high-quality contexts (for example R80/R66, R109/R107, R113/R106, R123/R120, R132/R133). Modifier probes did not establish a stable interaction, so PTEN loss should be interpreted as the robust predictor in this dataset rather than a context that necessarily modifies or is modified by other accepted markers.\\n6. CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency. Accepted signed contrasts are approximately 0.10 to 0.16, corresponding to raw more-negative MDM2 scores (R168/R177/R183/R178/R185/R209/R219/R234/R270). This finding should be narrowly interpreted because of eligibility selection, small exposed cells, and the broader inconsistency of KRAS-pathway predictors.
