Focus: low-screen-quality/low-Cas9 robustness for accepted SMARCA2, NFE2L2 reverse, USP7 reverse, WRN, STAT3, MDM2/CDKN2A, KRAS/NF1; new PI3K-AKT/MDM2 tests (PIK3CA and PTEN in TP53-intact high-quality); KEAP1-STAT3 plausible but uncertain; MTAP among CDKN2A-intact; PTEN interaction with CDKN2A-MDM2; adherent-culture robustness for SMARCA4-SMARCA2.","latest_stage_narratives":{"explore":"No assessments are due and no new validation budget remains, so this final exploration registers 12 internal probes only. All estimates are already signed to the registered direction. For direction -1, a positive signed mean difference means the exposed group is raw more negative, i.e. stronger dependency; for direction +1, a positive signed mean difference means the exposed group is raw less negative, i.e. weaker dependency. Interactions are signed to the registered direction, and practical importance is judged against roughly 10% of the absolute mean dependency score (about 0.025-0.030 for MDM2/STAT3/WRN/KRAS, 0.018 for USP7, 0.009 for NFE2L2, and 0.042 for SMARCA2).\n\nFirst, I registered low-screen-quality robustness checks for accepted core associations: PTEN loss/STAT3, CDKN2A loss/MDM2, KEAP1 loss/NFE2L2 reverse direction, TP53 loss/USP7 reverse direction, and NF1 loss/KRAS in KRAS-wild-type backgrounds. The aim is internal quality robustness, not external generalization. Similarly, MSI-high/WRN is checked under lower Cas9 activity to test whether the very large accepted association persists when editing efficiency is less favorable.\n\nSecond, I added a NRF2-pathway probe: KEAP1 loss versus STAT3 dependency under high screen quality and adequate Cas9 activity. KEAP1 loss is biologically plausible as a modifier of STAT3 through NRF2-driven oxidative-stress responses, but prior data do not establish direction. The registered direction +1 expresses the hypothesis that KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker STAT3 dependency, while anticipated_direction=0 reflects uncertainty and the risk that this is a null control.\n\nThird, I registered two PI3K-AKT/MDM2 pathway hypotheses: PIK3CA mutation and PTEN loss versus MDM2 dependency in high-quality, TP53-intact lines. PI3K/AKT activation can upregulate or functionally activate MDM2, and p53 wild-type status should make MDM2 dependency more meaningful. The registered direction -1 is stronger MDM2 dependency in the PI3K-activated exposure. These tests are specific because PIK3CA was not robust for STAT3/EGFR/ERBB2 outcomes and PTEN has a robust STAT3 association; if PTEN loss also shifts MDM2, that would broaden the dataset-specific PTEN signal.\n\nFourth, I probed CDKN2A/MDM2 context further: MTAP loss among CDKN2A-intact lines, and a high-quality interaction by PTEN loss. MTAP deletion often co-occurs with CDKN2A loss, and PTEN loss is a separate strong dependency predictor; both are registered as modifier or specificity probes with anticipated zero modification unless there is a meaningful interaction.\n\nFinally, I added an adherent-culture robustness check for SMARCA4 loss/SMARCA2 because growth/culture state can bias CRISPR screens and dependency measurements. This is not a new biological mechanism claim. All proposals remain dataset-specific associations, vulnerable to multiplicity, residual confounding, and selection effects, and none will be interpreted as causal or clinically generalizable without independent external replication.","analyze":"No assessments are due and the independent validation budget is exhausted, so I register no status changes and request analyses for the 12 remaining active untested claims, H293-H304. For direction +1 mean differences, positive evidence supports weaker dependency in the exposed group. For interactions, positive evidence supports a stronger registered effect in the named subgroup relative to its complement. I will assess acceptance using the roughly 10%-of-absolute-mean practical benchmark for each outcome, 95% interval exclusion of zero, and minimum cell sizes. I used approximately 10% of the absolute population mean dependency score as a practical benchmark, yielding roughly 0.025 for EGFR/RIT1/KIF18A, 0.028 for STAT3, 0.030 for WRN, 0.009 for NFE2L2, 0.042 for SMARCA2, and 0.018 for USP7. These are dataset-specific associations only; no causal, therapeutic, or external generalization is inferred. No validation was requested because the new validation budget is zero.\n\nH285 is rejected and closed. The EGFR-amplification-by-KRAS-wild-type interaction for dependency_EGFR gives a negative signed estimate of -0.0372 (95% CI -0.0949 to 0.0205), opposite the registered stronger-effect direction. The upper bound is below the EGFR practical benchmark of about 0.025, so there is no evidence for a clinically meaningful interaction in the registered direction. Because the interval still includes zero and the reversed interaction was not pre-specified as a new claim, I close this branch rather than propose a reversal.\n\nH286 is unresolved and closed. KRAS mutation versus KRAS wild type in high-screen-quality, high-Cas9, relatively clean co-mutation backgrounds gives a positive signed estimate of +0.0391 for dependency_RIT1, suggesting stronger RIT1 dependency among KRAS-mutant lines, but the interval (-0.0074 to 0.0855) crosses zero and exposed/comparator cells are modest. It is too uncertain to accept despite exceeding the RIT1 benchmark in the point estimate. This is consistent with the broader inconsistency of KRAS-mutation predictors and should not be expanded further.\n\nH287 is unresolved and closed. NF1 loss among KRAS-wild-type, high-screen-quality lines gives +0.0183 for dependency_RIT1, nominally in the predicted weaker-dependency direction, but the interval (-0.0283 to 0.0650) includes zero and the point estimate is below the RIT1 practical benchmark. This does not support a clinically meaningful RIT1 modification by NF1 loss in this context.\n\nH288 is unresolved and closed. MYC amplification in high-screen-quality, high-Cas9 backgrounds gives +0.0302 for dependency_KIF18A, above the KIF18A benchmark, but the interval (-0.0135 to 0.0740) includes zero and is imprecise. Given the prior broad null for MYC amplification across mitotic and transcriptional outcomes, this is a underpowered specificity probe, not a new accepted association.\n\nH289 is unresolved and closed. The PIK3CA-mutation interaction probe for PTEN-loss effects on dependency_STAT3 gives an estimate very close to zero, +0.0013 (95% CI -0.1499 to 0.1524). The point estimate suggests no meaningful modification of the accepted PTEN-loss/STAT3 association, but the interval is too wide to rule out a large interaction in either direction. This neither supports nor refutes a stable PI3K-pathway modifier; it leaves modifier uncertainty unresolved.\n\nH290 is rejected and closed as a specificity control. KEAP1 loss versus KEAP1 intact in high-screen-quality screens gives -0.0206 for dependency_WRN, opposite the registered weaker-dependency direction, with the positive upper bound (0.0201) below the WRN benchmark. record.narrative:
All estimates are interpreted as already signed to the registered hypothesis direction: for direction -1 mean differences, positive values indicate a raw more-negative dependency score in the exposed group, i.e. stronger dependency; for direction +1 mean differences, positive values indicate a raw less-negative score, i.e. weaker dependency. For interactions, positive values indicate a stronger registered effect in the named subgroup relative to its complement. I used roughly 10% of the absolute mean dependency score as a practical benchmark, approximately 0.028 for STAT3, 0.027 for MDM2, 0.009 for NFE2L2, 0.018 for USP7, 0.030 for WRN, 0.025 for KRAS, and 0.042 for SMARCA2. No validation was requested because the remaining new-validation budget is zero.

H293 is unresolved and closed. KEAP1 loss versus KEAP1 intact in high-screen-quality, adequate-Cas9 screens gives a near-zero signed STAT3 contrast, +0.0006 (95% CI -0.0418 to +0.0430). The point estimate is far below the STAT3 benchmark, but the interval still admits clinically meaningful values in both directions. This does not support a meaningful KEAP1-to-STAT3 association, but it is not precise enough to reject the possibility of a moderate modifier effect.

H294 is accepted and closed. PTEN loss versus PTEN intact among lower-screen-quality lines gives +0.300 (95% CI 0.216 to 0.383) for dependency_STAT3, far above the benchmark and excluding zero. This strongly supports the dataset-specific PTEN-loss/STAT3 association in a lower screen-quality subset. It remains an internal association, not evidence of causality or external generalizability.

H295 is accepted and closed. CDKN2A loss versus intact CDKN2A among lower-screen-quality lines gives +0.086 (95% CI 0.037 to 0.135) for dependency_MDM2, above the MDM2 benchmark and excluding zero. This supports the robustness of the CDKN2A-loss/MDM2 association when screen quality is lower. Because many related tests were performed, interpretation should remain conservative and association-specific.

H296 is accepted and closed. KEAP1 loss versus KEAP1 intact in lower-screen-quality lines gives +0.805 (95% CI 0.774 to 0.836) for dependency_NFE2L2, a very large effect far above the NFE2L2 benchmark. This robustly supports the accepted reverse-direction association: KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency in this dataset, not stronger dependency.

H297 is accepted and closed. TP53 loss versus intact TP53 in lower-screen-quality lines gives +0.341 (95% CI 0.219 to 0.463) for dependency_USP7, far above the USP7 benchmark. This supports the accepted reverse-direction association: TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency within this dataset.

H298 is accepted and closed, with cell-size caution. MSI-high versus non-MSI-high lines with lower Cas9 activity gives +0.798 (95% CI 0.732 to 0.864) for dependency_WRN. The exposed cell has only 27 observations, but it meets the minimum cell-size rule and the effect is extremely large and excludes zero. The MSI-high/WRN association therefore remains very strong under lower editing efficiency, though small exposed counts warrant caution.

H299 is unresolved and closed. NF1 loss versus NF1 intact among KRAS-wild-type, lower-screen-quality lines gives +0.012 (95% CI -0.043 to +0.066) for dependency_KRAS. The point estimate is below the KRAS benchmark and the interval includes both no effect and clinically meaningful effects. This does not support an accepted lower-quality KRAS-wild-type NF1 association.

H300 is rejected and closed. MTAP loss versus MTAP intact among CDKN2A-intact lines gives +0.004 (95% CI -0.018 to +0.026) for dependency_MDM2. The positive interval upper bound is below the MDM2 practical benchmark, so there is no evidence that MTAP loss acts as a meaningful independent modifier in this context. The estimate is essentially null.

H301 is unresolved and closed. The PTEN-loss interaction probe for CDKN2A-loss effects on dependency_MDM2 in high-quality screens gives +0.079 (95% CI -0.079 to +0.237). The point estimate is above benchmark, but the interval is too wide and crosses zero, and the exposed subgroup cell is small. The data cannot establish or exclude a clinically meaningful PTEN-dependent modification of the CDKN2A/MDM2 association.

H302 is rejected and closed. PIK3CA mutation versus wild type in high-quality, TP53-intact lines gives a negative signed MDM2 contrast, -0.025 (95% CI -0.065 to +0.015). The effect points opposite the registered stronger-dependency direction, and the upper bound is below the MDM2 benchmark. This provides no evidence for a meaningful PI3K-pathway association with MDM2 dependency in this setting.

H303 is unresolved and closed. PTEN loss versus intact in high-quality, TP53-intact lines gives a negative signed MDM2 contrast, -0.010 (95% CI -0.055 to +0.036). The point estimate is not meaningful, but the interval includes clinically meaningful positive values and zero, so a modest PTEN-to-MDM2 effect cannot be ruled out despite the negative point estimate.

H304 is accepted and closed. SMARCA4 loss versus intact among adherent cultures gives +0.788 (95% CI 0.765 to 0.811) for dependency_SMARCA2, far above the SMARCA2 benchmark. This supports the core SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 dependency association in the common adherent-culture subset. It remains a dataset-specific association and not a claim about causal synthetic lethality or clinical generalizability.

Overall, the low-screen-quality/low-Cas9 robustness checks support persistence of the major accepted associations for PTEN/STAT3, CDKN2A/MDM2, KEAP1/NFE2L2 reverse direction, TP53/USP7 reverse direction, MSI-high/WRN, and SMARCA4/SMARCA2. The remaining unresolved probes are limited by imprecision rather than by contradictory evidence. Multiplicity and residual confounding remain important caveats, especially for highly filtered or small-cell strata.

Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

The registered direction +1 expresses the hypothesis that KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker STAT3 dependency, while anticipated_direction=0 reflects uncertainty and the risk that this is a null control.\n\nThird, I registered two PI3K-AKT/MDM2 pathway hypotheses: PIK3CA mutation and PTEN loss versus MDM2 dependency in high-quality, TP53-intact lines. The registered direction -1 is stronger MDM2 dependency in the PI3K-activated exposure. These tests are specific because PIK3CA was not robust for STAT3/EGFR/ERBB2 outcomes and PTEN has a robust STAT3 association; if PTEN loss also shifts MDM2, that would broaden the dataset-specific PTEN signal.\n\nFourth, I probed CDKN2A/MDM2 context further: MTAP loss among CDKN2A-intact lines, and a high-quality interaction by PTEN loss. For interactions, positive values indicate a stronger registered effect in the named subgroup relative to its complement. I used roughly 10% of the absolute mean dependency score as a practical benchmark, approximately 0.028 for STAT3, 0.027 for MDM2, 0.009 for NFE2L2, 0.018 for USP7, 0.030 for WRN, 0.025 for KRAS, and 0.042 for SMARCA2. No validation was requested because the remaining new-validation budget is zero.\n\nH293 is unresolved and closed. KEAP1 loss versus KEAP1 intact in high-screen-quality, adequate-Cas9 screens gives a near-zero signed STAT3 contrast, +0.0006 (95% CI -0.0418 to +0.0430). The point estimate is far below the STAT3 benchmark, but the interval still admits clinically meaningful values in both directions. This does not support a meaningful KEAP1-to-STAT3 association, but it is not precise enough to reject the possibility of a moderate modifier effect.\n\nH294 is accepted and closed. PTEN loss versus PTEN intact among lower-screen-quality lines gives +0.300 (95% CI 0.216 to 0.383) for dependency_STAT3, far above the benchmark and excluding zero. This strongly supports the dataset-specific PTEN-loss/STAT3 association in a lower screen-quality subset. It remains an internal association, not evidence of causality or external generalizability.\n\nH295 is accepted and closed. CDKN2A loss versus intact CDKN2A among lower-screen-quality lines gives +0.086 (95% CI 0.037 to 0.135) for dependency_MDM2, above the MDM2 benchmark and excluding zero. This supports the robustness of the CDKN2A-loss/MDM2 association when screen quality is lower. Because many related tests were performed, interpretation should remain conservative and association-specific.\n\nH296 is accepted and closed. KEAP1 loss versus KEAP1 intact in lower-screen-quality lines gives +0.805 (95% CI 0.774 to 0.836) for dependency_NFE2L2, a very large effect far above the NFE2L2 benchmark. This robustly supports the accepted reverse-direction association: KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency in this dataset, not stronger dependency.\n\nH297 is accepted and closed. TP53 loss versus intact TP53 in lower-screen-quality lines gives +0.341 (95% CI 0.219 to 0.463) for dependency_USP7, far above the USP7 benchmark. This supports the accepted reverse-direction association: TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency within this dataset.\n\nH298 is accepted and closed, with cell-size caution. MSI-high versus non-MSI-high lines with lower Cas9 activity gives +0.798 (95% CI 0.732 to 0.864) for dependency_WRN. The exposed cell has only 27 observations, but it meets the minimum cell-size rule and the effect is extremely large and excludes zero. The MSI-high/WRN association therefore remains very strong under lower editing efficiency, though small exposed counts warrant caution.\n\nH299 is unresolved and closed. NF1 loss versus NF1 intact among KRAS-wild-type, lower-screen-quality lines gives +0.012 (95% CI -0.043 to +0.066) for dependency_KRAS. The point estimate is below the KRAS benchmark and the interval includes both no effect and clinically meaningful effects. This does not support an accepted lower-quality KRAS-wild-type NF1 association.\n\nH300 is rejected and closed. MTAP loss versus MTAP intact among CDKN2A-intact lines gives +0.004 (95% CI -0.018 to +0.026) for dependency_MDM2. A pre-specified replication model should estimate SMARCA4/SMARCA2, KEAP1/NFE2L2 reverse direction, TP53/USP7 reverse direction, MSI-high/WRN, PTEN/STAT3, CDKN2A/MDM2, and NF1-loss/KRAS-wild-type associations with adjustment for library, screen quality, Cas9 activity, lineage, ploidy, aneuploidy, mutation burden, proliferation, and co-occurring SMARCA4/ARID1A/KEAP1/TP53/MSI/PTEN/CDKN2A/MTAP/NF1/KRAS/EGFR/ERBB2 alterations, with multiplicity control and adequate cell sizes. If only internal analysis is possible, further work should be limited to the unresolved EGFR, KRAS-mutation, NF1-outside-context, and selected modifier hypotheses, using pre-registered contrasts and sample-size-aware reporting rather than broad subgroup exploration.
